statement: Accuracy register for the source reviewer. The reviewer is the curriculum foundation, not an authority: items here are flagged where it is outdated, contradicted by a current source, missing context, or needs verification. 'verified-issue' means the problem was confirmed against the cited external source; 'needs-verification' means a likely issue that has not yet been confirmed. A full line-by-line review of all 79 chapters has NOT been done — only targeted checks (chapters 1 [CLIA, prions], 26, 35, 40, Appendix B, and an automated scan).

scan.note: Automated scan (2026-10-07): 23 High-Yield/Number-Vault/Trap items cite a dated guideline, edition, or approval year and need a currency check; 134 High-Yield Hits use only/always/never wording and should be checked for overstatement when their lessons are built. The reviewer's own release record lists 22 items flagged for human review and a 34-item human-review queue that were not included in the EPUB.

flags.issue: Lists 'New York, D.C.' as CLIA-exempt alongside deemed accreditors. CMS's List of Exempt States names Washington (full exemption) and New York (partial exemption); D.C. is not listed. The trap's dodge also opens with 'Right', so the Trap/Dodge format is inverted here.

evidence.citation: CMS. List of Exempt States under CLIA, v. 08/15/2025

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-clia-complexity-accreditation teaches Washington (full) and New York (partial).

flags.issue: States that breath tests, noninvasive bilirubin and workplace drug tests are NOT regulated by CLIA. 42 CFR 493.3 excludes forensic-only testing, research not reporting patient results, and SAMHSA-certified drug testing; it does not list breath tests. Whether a given breath or noninvasive test falls under CLIA needs verification (e.g. against FDA/CMS categorization).

evidence.citation: 42 CFR 493.3 Applicability (eCFR)

flags.appAction: Lesson teaches only the regulation's exclusions.

flags.issue: Gives prion surface decontamination as ≥5,000 ppm hypochlorite (≈1:5–1:10 household bleach) or 1N NaOH (same in Exam Simulator key Q1). WHO (1999, Annex III) and CDC (reviewed 2026) give 2N NaOH or undiluted sodium hypochlorite for 1 hour for surfaces and heat-sensitive instruments; 20,000 ppm is the instrument-soak strength. The reviewer also says glutaraldehyde does 'not work', whereas WHO lists it as variably/partially effective (practical message unchanged).

evidence.citation: WHO Infection Control Guidelines for TSEs, WHO/CDS/CSR/APH/2000.3 (1999), Table 8 and Annex III
CDC. Infection Control for CJD (reviewed 2026-01-21)

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-prion-decontamination teaches the WHO/CDC surface method.

flags.issue: States 'eyewash within 100 ft' without the time criterion. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.151(c) requires suitable facilities 'within the work area for immediate emergency use' and sets no distance. A 1992 OSHA interpretation letter (construction) says equipment should be no more than 100 feet from the work station AND reachable within 10 seconds; later OSHA letters treat ANSI Z358.1 as non-enforceable guidance. The current ANSI/ISEA Z358.1 edition was not consulted.

evidence.citation: OSHA standard interpretation, July 20, 1992: Eyewash and shower equipment in construction
OSHA standard interpretation, Nov 1, 2002: Additional clarification of using ANSI Z358.1 as guidance to comply with 1910.151(c)

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-lab-design-hazcom-numbers teaches the regulation wording, the 10-second criterion and the 100-ft figure with its source.

flags.issue: Presents HazCom/GHS as the 2012 rule only; OSHA amended the standard again on May 20, 2024 (89 FR 44356). The SDS threshold wording ('>1%, carcinogens >0.1%') simplifies Appendix A mixture cut-off values: ≥1.0% for many health hazards and ≥0.1% for carcinogens (and Category 1 germ-cell mutagens). The SDS-in-English requirement is correct (1910.1200(g)(2)).

evidence.citation: 29 CFR 1910.1200 (eCFR, up to date as of 2026-10-05): (g)(2); Appendix A Tables A.5.1, A.6.1, A.8.3

flags.appAction: Lessons ops-lab-safety-precautions-osha (2024 update) and ops-lab-design-hazcom-numbers (cut-offs as ≥ values) teach the corrected wording.

flags.issue: Dates the bloodborne-pathogens standard to 1992; it was published in the Federal Register on December 6, 1991 (56 FR 64175). Also, OSHA's rule still requires 'universal precautions', while the reviewer says Standard Precautions replaced them (CDC terminology).

evidence.citation: 29 CFR 1910.1030 (eCFR) source note

flags.appAction: Lesson states the publication date and both terms.

flags.issue: States 35 ISBT blood group systems (>700 antigens). ISBT now registers 48 systems and 371 antigens (2025–2026 RCIBGT working-party report).

evidence.citation: ISBT Red Cell Immunogenetics and Blood Group Terminology Working Party, Annual Report 2025–2026

flags.appAction: Do not teach '35 systems'. Any lesson using this number must use the current ISBT count with a date.

flags.issue: Bibliography and Ch. 74 Hit 2 cite AABB Standards (2019). The current edition is the 35th, effective April 1, 2026 (two-year cycle). AABB-based statements (two ABO determinations, sample validity, parentage PI threshold) need re-checking against the current edition.

evidence.citation: AABB — Standards for Blood Banks and Transfusion Services (35th edition page)

flags.appAction: Claims sourced to AABB stay 'pending' until checked against the 35th edition.

flags.issue: Bibliography cites CLSI M100 '2020 edition per chapter notes'. M100 is revised annually; the current edition is M100-Ed36 (January 26, 2026). Any breakpoint values in Ch. 58 may be outdated.

evidence.citation: CLSI M100 — Performance Standards for Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing, 36th ed. (product page)

flags.appAction: Teach breakpoint concepts, not specific breakpoint numbers, unless checked against the current M100.

flags.issue: Cites WHO 2010 semen values (volume 2–5 mL, concentration 15–50 million/mL, total motility ≥40%, progressive ≥32%). The WHO manual 6th edition (2021) revised the lower 5th-centile limits (volume 1.4 mL, concentration 16 million/mL, total motility 42%, progressive 30%, normal forms 4%) and states the 5th centiles alone do not diagnose infertility. The reviewer's '2–5 mL' also does not match WHO 2010's lower limit (1.5 mL). Same issue in the Ch. 26 Number Vault.

evidence.citation: Boitrelle F, et al. The Sixth Edition of the WHO Manual for Human Semen Analysis: A Critical Review and SWOT Analysis. Life (Basel). 2021;11(12):1368. doi:10.3390/life11121368

flags.appAction: Use WHO 6th-edition values with the edition named, and note that they are reference centiles, not diagnostic cutoffs.

flags.issue: Gives the acute-leukemia blast threshold as ≥20% per WHO 2017. WHO-HAEM5 (2022) removed the 20% requirement for most AML with defining genetic abnormalities (exceptions such as BCR::ABL1 and CEBPA), and the 2022 ICC uses 10% for AML with defining genetic abnormalities. The threshold is classification-dependent.

evidence.citation: Haferlach T, et al. Overview on WHO-HAEM5 and the diagnostic relevance of genetic alterations for the classification. Medizinische Genetik. 2024;36:3. doi:10.1515/medgen-2024-2008

flags.appAction: Teach ≥20% as the classic rule with the genetic exceptions, and name the classification (WHO-HAEM5 vs ICC).

flags.issue: States '>62' Rh antigens. Not confirmed; the ISBT RH system antigen count should be checked against the current ISBT table.
flags.appAction: Avoid quoting this number until verified.

flags.issue: Core concept states MCHC is increased 'only' in spherocytosis. Dehydrated hereditary stomatocytosis (xerocytosis) also raises MCHC (Zama 2020); cold agglutinins raise it spuriously (Falvella 2021, La Gioia 2018), as can high bilirubin (Wu 2021); Falvella also links antiretroviral therapy and severe electrolyte disorders with increased MCHC. Wu 2021 found MCHC > 35.5 g/dL detected only 41% of hereditary spherocytosis cases.

evidence.citation: Zama D, et al. Ital J Pediatr. 2020;46:102 (abstract)
Falvella FS, et al. Scand J Clin Lab Invest. 2021;81(7):598-600 (abstract)
La Gioia A, et al. J Clin Pathol. 2018;71(8):729-734 (abstract)
Wu Y, Liao L, Lin F. J Clin Lab Anal. 2021;35(12):e24034

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-red-cell-indices-high-mchc teaches spherocytes and xerocytosis as true causes and cold agglutinins and interference as spurious causes.

flags.issue: Refers to '4 FDA-approved AD drugs'. Newer anti-amyloid antibodies have been approved since the older count; verify against current FDA approvals.
flags.appAction: Avoid a fixed count of approved drugs.

flags.issue: Uses the IUIS 2020 classification (430 disorders). IUIS publishes updates about every two years; verify the current count.
flags.appAction: State the count with its edition, or avoid it.

flags.issue: 'AABB requires two independent ABO determinations before transfusion' is a simplification of a requirement tied to how the second determination is obtained; verify wording in the current AABB Standards.
flags.appAction: ABO lesson words this as 'many standards require confirmation… check your laboratory's current standard' (pending claim cl-two-abo).

flags.issue: States ASCP weights of 17–22% for the four major areas. One secondary source gave 17–20% for Microbiology. The official ASCP guideline could not be retrieved to confirm.
flags.appAction: Track weights shown as unverified.

flags.issue: Regulatory content is US-specific (CLIA '88, OSHA, CMS/Medicare billing, FDA, AABB, Ch. 1 and 13). PH MTLE candidates need Philippine equivalents (R.A. 5527, DOH clinical laboratory licensing, etc.), which the reviewer does not cover.

evidence.citation: R.A. 5527 (Philippine Medical Technology Act of 1969)

flags.appAction: US-regulation lessons are tagged with a PH-context note; PH law concepts are listed as gap domain gap-ph-law.

flags.issue: 'Twelve states plus Puerto Rico require lab personnel licensure' matches a university program list dated June 2017 (CA, FL, GA, HI, LA, MT, NV, NY, ND, RI, TN, WV + PR). The count can change and should be re-checked against current state law.

evidence.citation: University of Minnesota, Medical Laboratory Sciences: Certification and Licensure (list current as of June 2017)

flags.appAction: Taught as a dated count with a pending claim.

flags.issue: 'Rooms >100 sq ft need two exits' and the HVAC targets (68–76 °F, 20–60% humidity, 12 air changes/hour) could not be matched to a consulted code or standard; exit and ventilation requirements depend on the fire and building codes and design standards in force.
flags.appAction: Taught only as the reviewer’s design targets, with pending claims.

flags.issue: '~25 sharps injuries per 100 average daily census (2014)' and 'up to $5,000 per incident' were not found in the sources consulted. A Massachusetts surveillance report gives 16.2 per 100 licensed beds for 2014 (a different denominator).

evidence.citation: Massachusetts DPH. Sharps injuries among hospital workers in Massachusetts, 2014 (search-result summary only; report not read in full)

flags.appAction: Taught as the reviewer’s figures with pending claims.

flags.issue: Presents EDTA carry-over from wrong order of draw as certain. The order itself matches WHO 2010, but a closed-system study (Ercan 2021) found no detectable K-EDTA contamination from incorrect order in routine workflow; contamination is still reported in practice (Lima-Oliveira 2014 cites it as the cause of 14.3% of hypocalcaemia cases). The reviewer also omits that skin punctures reverse the order.

evidence.citation: WHO guidelines on drawing blood (2010), Table 2.3 and section 7.1.3
Ercan Ş et al. Biochem Med (Zagreb). 2021;31(2):020704
Lima-Oliveira G et al. Biochem Med (Zagreb). 2014;24(3):359-367

flags.appAction: Lesson pre-order-of-draw-edta teaches the order, the mixed evidence and the reversed skin-puncture order.

flags.issue: States fluoride 'good for 3 days'. WHO 2010 (Table 2.3) says oxalate/fluoride 'preserves glucose up to five days'. The reviewer also omits citrate-buffered tubes, which act immediately and are advised by AACC/ADA when samples cannot be cooled and separated within 30 minutes (as quoted in Gupta 2016).

evidence.citation: WHO guidelines on drawing blood (2010), Table 2.3
Gupta S et al. Int J Appl Basic Med Res. 2016;6(1):50-53

flags.appAction: Lesson pre-tube-additives-fluoride-gel keeps the stability duration pending and teaches citrate-buffered tubes.

flags.issue: Attributes 'wrong test/panel selection is the most frequent preanalytic error' to Bonini 2002, whose abstract does not state this. '~1 in 12,000 patients get blood intended for someone else' does not match Linden 2000's abstract (1 in 19,000 RBC units administered in error). '~1 in 1,000 specimens misidentified' and WBIT 1.1 vs 2.7 per 1,000 were not found in sources read; one large hospital reported 0.0511% (≈1 in 2,000) before interventions.

evidence.citation: Bonini P et al. Clin Chem. 2002;48(5):691-698 (abstract)
Linden JV et al. Transfusion. 2000;40(10):1207-1213 (abstract)
Ning HC et al. PLoS One. 2016;11(8):e0160821

flags.appAction: Lesson pre-patient-id-wbit teaches published figures and keeps the reviewer’s as pending.

flags.issue: Cites only the FDA 2017 biotin safety communication. FDA issued an update on November 5, 2019 and maintains a page listing troponin assays that have not addressed biotin interference (reports of falsely low troponin). The reviewer also omits the direction of error (sandwich assays falsely low, competitive assays falsely high).

evidence.citation: FDA. Biotin interference with troponin lab tests — assays subject to biotin interference
Fan J et al. BCMJ. 2019;61(2):66-71

flags.appAction: Lesson pre-biotin-daratumumab-interference teaches both communications and the direction of error.

flags.issue: States 'first-morning void is best for cytology'. Reference-laboratory instructions state a first-morning voided specimen is not suitable for urine cytology and prefer a second-morning specimen; first-morning urine is preferred for chemical analysis (Caleffi 2010). The urobilinogen 2–4 pm timing was not verified.

evidence.citation: Labcorp. Urine cytology (test 009068) specimen information
Caleffi A et al. Biochem Med (Zagreb). 2010;20(2):179-183

flags.appAction: Lesson pre-allen-test-urine-timing teaches second-morning urine for cytology.

flags.issue: Number Vault gives heel lancet depth '≤2 mm'. WHO 2010 (7.1.2) says heel-prick depth should not go beyond 2.4 mm and advises avoiding the posterior heel (2.33 mm to bone in a 3-kg baby). The 2 mm figure may come from another guideline that was not consulted.

evidence.citation: WHO guidelines on drawing blood (2010), section 7.1.2

flags.appAction: Lesson pre-specimen-numbers-rcf-24h-urine teaches WHO’s 2.4 mm with the reviewer’s 2 mm noted.

flags.issue: Number Vault gives 'arterial gas transport 1–5 °C ice water'. Sources disagree: WHO 2010 places the syringe in an ice cup, while Sood 2010 says do not cool and analyse within 30 minutes. Practice depends on syringe type and lab policy.

evidence.citation: WHO guidelines on drawing blood (2010), section 5.2.2
Sood P et al. Indian J Crit Care Med. 2010;14(2):57-64

flags.appAction: Lesson pre-specimen-numbers-rcf-24h-urine presents the disagreement and defers to lab policy.

flags.issue: States 'serum ferritin <12 μg/L is diagnostic' and that in inflammation '<50–60 μg/L predicts likely response to iron'. WHO 2020 recommends <15 µg/L for iron deficiency in apparently healthy children over 5, adolescents and adults, and <70 µg/L in adults (<30 µg/L in children) with infection or inflammation. Weiss 2019 associates ferritin <30 µg/L with true iron deficiency. Cut-offs are guideline-dependent.

evidence.citation: WHO guideline on use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status (2020), recommendations 1.1–1.2 and Table 1
Weiss G, Ganz T, Goodnough LT. Blood. 2019;133(1):40-50

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-microcytic-anemia-ferritin-mentzer teaches WHO 2020 cut-offs and lists the reviewer’s as pending.

flags.issue: States the tube coagulase test is '~100% sensitive'. The ASM protocol calls the tube test definitive but gives no sensitivity figure; no source read for this app supports ~100%.

evidence.citation: Katz DS. Coagulase Test Protocol. American Society for Microbiology; 2010 (revised 2016)

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-gpc-catalase-coagulase-mrsa says only that the tube test is definitive and lists the figure as pending.

flags.issue: Hit 3 reads 'tube coagulase … positive = S. aureus'. ASM notes S. schleiferi and S. intermedius may also be tube-positive (and S. lugdunensis and S. schleiferi slide-positive). Hit 21 partly qualifies this ('clinically relevant coagulase-positive staphylococcus').

evidence.citation: Katz DS. Coagulase Test Protocol. American Society for Microbiology; 2010 (revised 2016)

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-gpc-catalase-coagulase-mrsa teaches the exceptions.

flags.issue: States that after a fever rise of ≥1 °C the transfusion must never be restarted until evaluated, and that febrile non-hemolytic reactions last 2–3 h. WHO 2001 (Clinical Use of Blood) allows restarting slowly with a new unit if the patient improves; the CDC NHSN Hemovigilance protocol v3.0 (2026) no longer defines febrile non-hemolytic reactions. The ≥1 °C threshold and 2–3 h course were not found in the sources read.

evidence.citation: WHO. The Clinical Use of Blood: Handbook. 2001, pp. 61–67
CDC NHSN Biovigilance Component Hemovigilance Module Protocol v3.0, January 2026

flags.appAction: Lesson bb-acute-hemolytic-reaction-abo-compatibility teaches only “stop and rule out hemolysis and bacterial contamination”.

flags.issue: States FENa > 1% suggests acute tubular necrosis. The 2025 European Journal of Heart Failure consensus (Table 2) treats FeNa 1–2% as indeterminate and > 2% as intrinsic; it and a 2026 BMJ Open meta-analysis also note that diuretics push FeNa above 1% even in prerenal states.

evidence.citation: Kobayashi M, et al. Eur J Heart Fail. 2025;27(11):2372-2396, Table 2
Pan HC, et al. BMJ Open. 2026;16:e100875

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-fena-prerenal-vs-atn teaches < 1% / 1–2% / > 2% bands and the diuretic limitation.

flags.issue: States two blood-culture sets catch 80%, three 96% and four 100% of bacteremias (also in the Number Vault). These are Cockerill 2004 figures; Lee 2007 found 73.1%, 89.7%, 98.2% and 99.8% for one to four cultures. No source shows four sets detect 100%.

evidence.citation: Lee A, Mirrett S, Reller LB, Weinstein MP. J Clin Microbiol. 2007;45(11):3546-3548 (abstract)

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-blood-culture-volume-contamination teaches the Lee 2007 yields and mentions the earlier figures.

flags.issue: States blood-culture sets are drawn 30–60 minutes apart (also in the Number Vault). CDC guidance says at least two sets within a few hours of each other (within 24 h) from separate venipuncture sites, and its worked example uses sets drawn within 5 minutes; no fixed 30–60-minute interval was found.

evidence.citation: CDC. Blood Culture Contamination: An Overview for Infection Control and Antibiotic Stewardship Programs. 2022 (rev. 2023)
CDC. Collect Adult Blood Culture Sets. Updated 2026 Mar 31

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-blood-culture-volume-contamination teaches 'within a few hours, separate sites'.

flags.issue: States HBV becomes chronic in 80% of neonates and 1–2% of adolescents/adults. CDC (2025) gives about 90% of infected infants, 30% of children infected at 1–5 years and about 5% of adults (95% recover); Kumar 2023 gives ~95% perinatal, 20–30% at 1–5 years, < 5% adults.

evidence.citation: CDC. Clinical Overview of Hepatitis B. Updated 2025 Aug 29
Kumar M, et al. Diagnostics (Basel). 2023;13(3):368

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-hepatitis-b-serology-window teaches the CDC figures.

flags.issue: Calls IgM anti-HBc the 'sole marker' of the core window. Total anti-HBc (which includes IgM) is also positive in that phase (Patel 2024, Table 2), and HBV DNA can be detected in the window period (Kumar 2023). The practical point — test IgM anti-HBc — is correct.

evidence.citation: Patel A, et al. Gastro Hep Adv. 2024;3(2):139, Table 2
Kumar M, et al. Diagnostics (Basel). 2023;13(3):368, Table 2

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-hepatitis-b-serology-window says 'anti-HBc, including IgM, is positive and HBV DNA may be detectable'.

flags.issue: States multiplex viral NAATs are 'the standard of care for respiratory viruses'. The IDSA 2018 influenza guideline recommends molecular assays over antigen tests broadly, but recommends multiplex RT-PCR respiratory panels specifically for hospitalized immunocompromised patients. Other pathogens and newer guidance were not checked.

evidence.citation: Uyeki TM, et al. Clin Infect Dis. 2019;68(6):e1-e47, recommendations 10–12

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-respiratory-virus-naat-antigen-culture teaches the narrower IDSA recommendation.

flags.issue: Gives removal as Y = Y₀·e⁻ˣ but states 30% remains after one plasma volume and 10% after two; e⁻¹ ≈ 37% and e⁻² ≈ 14%. Bauer 2022 reports the first session removes 65–70% of an intravascular substance, the second about 23% more and the third about 9% more.

evidence.citation: Bauer PR, et al. Intensive Care Med. 2022;48(10):1382

flags.appAction: Lesson ih-plasma-exchange-tpe teaches Bauer 2022's per-session figures.

flags.issue: Gives 2.5 × 10⁶ CD34⁺ cells/kg as the minimal engraftment dose. De Clercq 2019 cites a minimum threshold of ≥ 2 × 10⁶ CD34⁺/kg for autologous PBSC transplantation. Thresholds differ by program and transplant type; the reviewer's figure was not found in the sources read.

evidence.citation: De Clercq E. Antivir Chem Chemother. 2019;27:2040206619829382

flags.appAction: Lesson ih-hpc-cd34-dose-cryopreservation teaches ≥ 2 × 10⁶/kg and shows the reviewer's 2.5 × 10⁶/kg.

flags.issue: Defines a dilute specimen as creatinine ≤ 20 mg/dL and SG ≤ 1.0030. The US DOT laboratory criteria (49 CFR 40.88) are creatinine ≥ 2 and < 20 mg/dL with SG > 1.0010 and < 1.0030; values below those floors fall in the substituted or invalid range. Argoff 2018 uses ≤ 20 mg/dL and ≤ 1.003 as clinical tampering flags, so the reviewer’s numbers match clinical screening practice but not the regulatory definition.

evidence.citation: Argoff CE, et al. Pain Med. 2018;19(1):97-117

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-drug-screen-confirmation-validity teaches the DOT criteria with lower bounds and labels them as US federal rules.

flags.issue: Lists “temperature outside 90–100 °F” among the criteria for a substituted specimen. Under 49 CFR 40.65, temperature (32–38 °C / 90–100 °F, read within 4 minutes) is a collection-site check; an out-of-range reading triggers an immediate new collection under direct observation, and both specimens are sent. “Substituted” is a laboratory result based on creatinine and specific gravity (40.88).
flags.appAction: Lesson chem-drug-screen-confirmation-validity teaches temperature as a collection check and includes a trap card and a question on it.

flags.issue: States BNP “does NOT rise” in TRALI and that TRALI gets “oxygen only”. The 2019 consensus redefinition says natriuretic peptides are always elevated in critically ill patients and severe TRALI (hypoxic vasoconstriction), so they help mainly in milder cases; a low BNP (< 300 pg/mL) or NT-proBNP (< 2,000 pg/mL) argues against TACO. TRALI care is supportive and includes mechanical ventilation when needed; avoiding diuretics is supported.

evidence.citation: Vlaar APJ, et al. Transfusion. 2019;59(7):2465-2476
Kuriri FA. Saudi Med J. 2025;46(8):865-877

flags.appAction: Lesson bb-trali-vs-taco teaches BNP as a rule-out for TACO, notes it is raised in severe TRALI, and teaches supportive care including ventilation.

flags.issue: States a direct (homogeneous) LDL-C assay “stays valid even at TG 600” when Friedewald cannot be used. HEART UK/ACB (Kenkre 2025) reports marked, clinically relevant bias of direct LDL-c versus the CDC reference method, says performance is method-dependent and does not recommend direct LDL-c in hypertriglyceridaemic samples (suggesting apoB); Wolska 2026 notes direct assays on dyslipidaemic samples can be substantially lower or higher than beta-quantification. Non-HDL-C, Sampson–NIH (to TG 800 mg/dL) or extended Martin–Hopkins are the supported alternatives.

evidence.citation: Kenkre JS, et al. Ann Clin Biochem. 2025;62(4):257-286
Wolska A, et al. Curr Atheroscler Rep. 2026;28(1):27

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-ldl-calculation-friedewald teaches non-HDL-C, Sampson–NIH, Martin–Hopkins and apoB, and cautions that direct LDL-C can be biased at high TG.

flags.issue: States enzyme treatment (ficin/papain) destroys S/s along with Fyᵃ/Fyᵇ, M and N. Manduzio 2024 states S and s show a variable effect with enzymes (M, N and Duffy destroyed; Kell unaffected). Effects may differ between papain and ficin and between methods; a second source was not read.

evidence.citation: Manduzio P. Hematol Rep. 2024;16(4):815-824

flags.appAction: Lesson ih-antibody-id-dosage-kidd teaches S/s as variable with ficin.

flags.issue: Presents a fixed hCG discriminatory zone of 1500–2000 mIU/mL above which a sac “should” be seen, with no sac suggesting ectopic. Bobdiwala 2017 says the zone should not be used to time scans or to make a presumptive diagnosis of ectopic pregnancy, that most ectopics are seen at hCG < 1,000 IU/L, and that basing methotrexate on it is dangerous; Pereira 2019 notes the value varies by centre and equipment (their protocol uses 3,500 mIU/mL).

evidence.citation: Bobdiwala S, et al. Womens Health (Lond). 2017;13(2):27-33
Pereira PP, et al. Clinics (Sao Paulo). 2019;74:e1111

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-hcg-pregnancy-unknown-location teaches the zone as a guide that varies and never diagnoses ectopic pregnancy alone.

flags.issue: Uses “rising < 53% in 2 days = abnormal (99% sensitive)”. A later study of 1,249 PUL patients set the minimal 48-h rise for a viable intrauterine pregnancy at 35% (99.9% CI); the 53% threshold can misclassify viable pregnancies (Pereira 2019; Nwabuobi 2017).

evidence.citation: Pereira PP, et al. Clinics (Sao Paulo). 2019;74:e1111
Nwabuobi C, et al. Int J Mol Sci. 2017;18(10):2037

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-hcg-pregnancy-unknown-location teaches the 35% minimum rise and shows the older 53% figure as a trap.

flags.issue: States platelets are stored “up to 5 days” (also in the Number Vault and simulator explanation). Room-temperature platelet storage is now 5–7 days where bacterial-risk controls (e.g. pathogen reduction) are used, and an FDA 2023 variance allows cold-stored platelets for up to 14 days at 1–6 °C for active bleeding (Akaraphanth 2026; Cancelas 2022).

evidence.citation: Akaraphanth M, et al. Transfusion. 2026;66(Suppl 1):S350-S367
Cancelas JA, et al. Transfusion. 2022;62(8):1619-1629

flags.appAction: Lesson bb-component-storage-irradiation teaches 5–7 days at 20–24 °C with agitation and mentions licensed cold-stored platelets as the exception.

flags.issue: States end-of-storage platelet pH “must be ≥ 6.0”. A 2022 US licensing study used pH (22 °C) ≥ 6.2 as the acceptance endpoint (Cancelas 2022). The current AABB/FDA criterion was not read directly, so this stays unconfirmed.

evidence.citation: Cancelas JA, et al. Transfusion. 2022;62(8):1619-1629

flags.appAction: Not taught as a number in lessons until the current standard is confirmed.

flags.issue: States acromegaly “is diagnosed by” failure of GH to suppress below 1 ng/mL during an OGTT. The 2024 Acromegaly Consensus confirms the diagnosis with IGF-I > 1.3 × ULN for age plus characteristic clinical signs; random GH is not required, and the OGTT is reserved for equivocal results (Giustina 2024; De Marinis 2026).

evidence.citation: Giustina A, et al. Pituitary. 2024;27(1):7-22
De Marinis L, et al. Pituitary. 2026;29(2):67

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-endocrine-dynamic-testing teaches IGF-I first, with the OGTT for equivocal cases.

flags.issue: States chlamydiae are “energy parasites” with no cytochromes that “can’t make ATP”. Current reviews: reticulate bodies scavenge host ATP, but elementary bodies generate ATP from glucose-6-phosphate and amino acids, and C. trachomatis can make ATP via a sodium gradient — the 1960s–70s energy-parasite hypothesis has been challenged (Mandel 2024; Cheong 2023).

evidence.citation: Mandel CG, et al. Front Cell Infect Microbiol. 2024;14:1284701
Cheong HC, et al. Microorganisms. 2023;11(6):1382

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-chlamydia-mycoplasma-diagnosis teaches host-ATP dependence of RBs and flags “no ATP at all” as a trap.

flags.issue: Presents azithromycin 1 g single dose and doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days as equivalent first-line options for genital chlamydia. The CDC 2021 STI guidelines recommend doxycycline for 7 days; azithromycin 1 g is an alternative regimen (Workowski 2021).

evidence.citation: Workowski KA, et al. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2021;70(4):1-187

flags.appAction: Not taught as treatment in lessons; noted here for learners.

flags.issue: Lists “osmotic fragility increased” alongside EMA binding as the HS tests without noting that the conventional osmotic fragility test is no longer recommended (low sensitivity and specificity, poor standardisation); flow-based osmotic fragility and EMA binding are preferred (Chueh 2022 Korean guideline).

evidence.citation: Chueh HW, et al. Blood Res. 2022;57(2):86-94

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-hemolytic-anemia-workup teaches EMA binding and flow-based OFT, and flags conventional OFT as a trap.

flags.issue: Defines acute pancreatitis as “clinical features + amylase/lipase >3× the upper reference limit”. The revised Atlanta classification requires at least two of three — typical abdominal pain, amylase and/or lipase ≥ 3 × ULN, characteristic imaging — so enzyme elevation is not mandatory (Varlamov 2026; Lázár 2026).

evidence.citation: Varlamov D, et al. BMC Gastroenterol. 2026;26(1):561
Lázár B, et al. Front Cell Infect Microbiol. 2026;16:1808503

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-pancreatic-enzymes-pancreatitis teaches the 2-of-3 rule.

flags.issue: States “morulae in NEUTROPHILS = Anaplasma phagocytophilum; Ehrlichia targets MONOCYTES.” CDC notes Ehrlichia ewingii has a predilection for granulocytes and forms morulae there, and that smear findings need confirmatory testing (Biggs 2016).

evidence.citation: Biggs HM, et al. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2016;65(2):1-44

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-rickettsial-tickborne-diagnosis teaches granulocytic morulae as Anaplasma or E. ewingii, confirmed by PCR/serology.

flags.issue: Gives a red-cell trigger of “< 8.0 g/dL in acute coronary syndrome”. The MINT trial (acute MI, n = 3504) found a restrictive 7–8 g/dL strategy associated with more MI or death than a liberal 10 g/dL strategy (HR 1.15), so a fixed restrictive trigger in acute MI is contested (Yang 2026).

evidence.citation: Yang H, et al. Front Med (Lausanne). 2026;13:1762664

flags.appAction: Lesson bb-component-choice-thresholds teaches 7 g/dL for most stable patients and acute MI as an exception favouring a more liberal approach.

flags.issue: Gives cryoprecipitate when fibrinogen < 100 mg/dL with bleeding, and ~150–250 mg fibrinogen per unit. Current reviews put increased bleeding risk below ~200 mg/dL (population-dependent), trials enrol at < 200 mg/dL, and the AABB standard is ≥ 150 mg fibrinogen per unit (US single units often ~700 mg per American Red Cross) (Rahe-Meyer 2026; Hess 2026).

evidence.citation: Rahe-Meyer N, et al. J Clin Med. 2026;15(16):6156
Hess AS, et al. Transfusion. 2026;66(7):1424-1437

flags.appAction: Lesson bb-component-choice-thresholds says risk rises below ~200 mg/dL and that triggers vary.

flags.issue: Gives mild hemophilia as 6–30% factor activity. The standard classification is severe < 1 IU/dL, moderate 1–5, mild > 5–40 IU/dL (Alvarez-Payares 2026, citing the ISTH/WFH classification).

evidence.citation: Alvarez-Payares JC, et al. Cureus. 2026;18(4):e106284

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-hemophilia-factor-inhibitor-lab teaches > 5–40 IU/dL and shows 6–30% as a trap.

flags.issue: Built on the Fourth Universal Definition of MI (2018) with numbered MI types (e.g., type 4a, type 5) and sex-specific cut-offs only “when provided”. The Fifth Universal Definition (2026) requires sex-specific 99th percentile URLs and replaces the numbered types with primary, secondary and procedure-related MI (Mills 2026).

evidence.citation: Mills NL, et al. Glob Heart. 2026;21(1):64

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-troponin-myocardial-injury teaches the 2026 definition; numbered types are not taught.

flags.issue: States that against metallo-β-lactamase producers “aztreonam stays active”. MBLs cannot hydrolyse aztreonam, but many MBL producers co-express ESBL and/or AmpC enzymes that inactivate it, which is why aztreonam is combined with avibactam (Khan 2026).

evidence.citation: Khan M, et al. Front Microbiol. 2026;17:1913726

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-beta-lactamases-esbl-cpe teaches the co-production caveat as a trap.

flags.issue: Presents nitrocefin as the way to catch β-lactamase hidden behind a susceptible MIC in staphylococci. In a blaZ-confirmed study (S. saprophyticus) nitrocefin was the least sensitive phenotypic test (28.9%) and the zone-edge test the most sensitive (90.3%); combined testing performed best (Ferreira 2017). Generalisability to S. aureus was not verified.

evidence.citation: Ferreira AM, et al. Braz J Microbiol. 2017;48(1):159-166

flags.appAction: Lesson says a negative nitrocefin test does not rule out penicillinase.

flags.issue: States the 12.5 g/dL / 38% hemoglobin minimum “applies to ALL whole-blood donors”. Under 21 CFR 630.10, 12.5 g/dL / 38% is the female allogeneic minimum (12.0–12.5 permitted under an FDA-acceptable procedure); male allogeneic donors need ≥ 13.0 g/dL / 39%. The checklist also omits the lower BP limits (systolic ≥ 90, diastolic ≥ 50 mmHg).

evidence.citation: 21 CFR 630.10 (eCFR, accessed 2026-10-08)

flags.appAction: Lesson bb-donor-eligibility-criteria teaches sex-specific minimums and full BP limits.

flags.issue: Calls Enterococcus a “bacitracin-resistant + PYR-positive beta-hemolytic streptococcus”. Enterococcus is a separate genus, and most isolates are not β-hemolytic (β-hemolysis in 20.3% of 74 isolates in one 2026 study, on horse blood). The PYR/bacitracin answer stands, but identification should rest on growth in 6.5% NaCl and a positive bile esculin test, not on β-hemolysis.

evidence.citation: Fialho N, et al. Antibiotics (Basel). 2026;15(7):657
Gajic I, et al. Int J Mol Sci. 2026;27(11):5092 (Table 4)

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-strep-enterococcus-id teaches that most enterococci are γ and confirms Enterococcus by 6.5% NaCl and bile esculin.

flags.issue: States that “HPCs do not express ABO antigens (they engraft in ABO-incompatible recipients)”. Matteocci 2024 states that ABO antigens are present on hematopoietic stem cells. The clinical conclusion (ABO incompatibility is not a contraindication; incompatible red cells or plasma in the product are reduced) is supported, but the mechanism given conflicts with the source read. Primary studies of ABO expression on CD34⁺ cells were not read.

evidence.citation: Matteocci A, Pierelli L. Cells. 2024;13(10):814

flags.appAction: Lesson ih-hpc-graft-sources-abo teaches only that ABO mismatch is not a contraindication and how the product is manipulated; the expression claim is not taught.

flags.issue: Uses a VWF activity/antigen ratio of ≥ 0.6 vs < 0.6 to separate type 1 from type 2, and (Memory Hooks) a FVIII:C/VWF:Ag ratio < 0.6 for type 2N. The ASH ISTH NHF WFH 2021 guideline, as summarized by Tosetto & Eikenboom 2026, suggests < 0.7 to confirm type 2 (low certainty) and uses FVIII/VWF:Ag < 0.7 to prompt testing for 2N or mild hemophilia A. Cut-offs remain lab- and assay-dependent.

evidence.citation: Tosetto A, Eikenboom J. Haematologica. 2026;111(1):35-43

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-vwd-typing-ratios teaches the < 0.7 cut-offs and notes the low certainty.

flags.issue: Gives the normal anion gap as “≈ 12 mEq/L (8–16)”. That range dates from flame-photometry sodium and colorimetric chloride; ion-selective electrodes shifted the normal gap to about 6 ± 3 mEq/L (Lee 2006), and a 2025 review lists 4–12 mmol/L. The normal range is method-dependent and should be taken from the performing laboratory.

evidence.citation: Lee S, Kang KP, Kang SK. Electrolyte Blood Press. 2006;4(1):44-46
Korus J, et al. Diagnostics (Basel). 2025;15(16):2052

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-anion-gap-delta-osmolal teaches method-dependent ranges and “use your lab’s range”.

flags.issue: Says sputum is “rejected if > 10 squamous epithelial cells/LPF” but “acceptable if < 25 epithelial cells AND > 25 neutrophils/LPF” — a specimen with 11–24 SEC would be both rejected and acceptable. The criterion read (Dong 2026) is acceptable with < 10 SEC and > 25 leukocytes per LPF; > 10 SEC indicates oropharyngeal contamination. Some scoring systems differ; laboratories set their own criteria.

evidence.citation: Dong K, et al. Front Microbiol. 2026;17:1894814

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-specimen-acceptability-transport teaches < 10 SEC and > 25 WBC per LPF.

flags.issue: States that the HBV “core window” (HBsAg cleared, anti-HBs not yet present) “is caught by HBV NAT — why NAT is in the required donor screening panel”. Badawi 2025 describes the core-window gap as the period when anti-HBc may be the only positive marker; NAT’s documented role is shortening the early window (HBV DNA detectable on average 6–15 days before HBsAg) and detecting occult infection. The reviewer’s own simulator (Q190, Q579) correctly ties the core window to anti-HBc.

evidence.citation: Badawi MA, et al. Viruses. 2025;18(1):23

flags.appAction: Lesson ih-dhtr-lookback-windows teaches NAT for the early window and anti-HBc for the core window.

flags.issue: States “RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs = glomerular disease, full stop.” RBC casts are usually glomerular (nephritic syndrome), but a biopsy study cited by Gaggar 2024 found RBC casts in 29% of acute interstitial nephritis; acanthocytes and dysmorphic RBCs are relatively specific but insensitive markers.

evidence.citation: Gaggar P, Raju SB. Indian J Nephrol. 2024;34(3):213-221

flags.appAction: Lesson cm-urine-casts-localize teaches RBC casts as usually glomerular, with the interstitial-nephritis exception.

flags.issue: Ties waxy and broad casts to end-stage kidney disease and WBC casts to pyelonephritis. Gaggar 2024 lists waxy casts in renal failure, acute as well as chronic, and WBC casts in acute interstitial nephritis and nephritic syndrome as well as pyelonephritis.

evidence.citation: Gaggar P, Raju SB. Indian J Nephrol. 2024;34(3):213-221

flags.appAction: Lesson cm-urine-casts-localize teaches the broader associations.

flags.issue: States PV has “JAK2 V617F in essentially all cases”. JAK2 V617F is found in > 95% of PV; the remaining 3–5% carry non-canonical JAK2 mutations (exons 12–15), which the WHO/ICC 2022 criteria accept. A V617F-negative result therefore does not exclude PV.

evidence.citation: Palandri F, et al. Ann Hematol. 2026;105(5):251
Testa U, et al. Med Sci (Basel). 2026;14(5):552

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-mpn-pv-et-pmf teaches V617F > 95% and exon 12–15 testing when V617F is negative.

flags.issue: Gives PMF “median survival ~5 years”. Shao 2025 cites an overall median survival of 9.2 years (15- and 20-year survival 32% and 20%); survival varies widely with risk score.

evidence.citation: Shao R, et al. Cancers (Basel). 2025;18(1):50

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-mpn-pv-et-pmf cites ≈ 9 years in one large series.

flags.issue: Hit 3 gives homozygous factor V Leiden ~10–15× VTE risk and Hit 9 / the Number Vault give FVL heterozygote + OCPs 8–20×, while the reviewer’s own Ch. 72 simulator question and explanation cite ~7× heterozygous and ~80× homozygous. Published figures differ: Khider 2022 gives ~5× heterozygous and ~10× homozygous; Nakashima & Rogers 2014 give 4–8× heterozygous, 80× homozygous and 30–60× for heterozygotes on oral contraceptives.

evidence.citation: Nakashima MO, Rogers HJ. Blood Res. 2014;49(2):85-94
Khider L, Gendron N, Mauge L. Int J Mol Sci. 2022;23(3):1821

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-thrombophilia-testing-timing teaches that risks combine and that fold-increases vary by study, without single combined numbers; simulator question with the 80-fold figure carries a note.

flags.issue: Hit 4 and the “Hapto-goblin” memory hook say myoglobin does not bind haptoglobin. Two rhabdomyolysis reviews state that circulating myoglobin is normally bound to plasma globulins, mainly haptoglobin. The diagnostic contrast (low haptoglobin in hemolysis; very high CK in rhabdomyolysis) is not in question, but the binding claim needs a primary binding study.

evidence.citation: Petejova N, Martinek A. Crit Care. 2014;18(3):224
Gupta A, Thorson P, Penmatsa KR, Gupta P. Ulster Med J. 2021;90(2):61-69

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-plasma-protein-patterns separates hemoglobinuria and myoglobinuria by haptoglobin/LD vs CK and does not teach the binding claim.

flags.issue: Trap 2 calls bisalbuminemia a benign heterozygous variant (slower band) needing no work-up. Hereditary bisalbuminemia is permanent and benign, but an acquired, transient form with a faster band occurs with high-dose β-lactam antibiotics and pancreatic pseudocyst.

evidence.citation: Kapatia G, et al. J Lab Physicians. 2021;13(3):219-223

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-plasma-protein-patterns teaches hereditary vs acquired bisalbuminemia.

flags.issue: Hit 9 and Trap 4 present piperacillin-tazobactam as a current cause of false-positive galactomannan (“FDA says disclose it”). The false positives came from galactomannan-contaminated lots; a 2014 multicentre US study found no galactomannan in 32 current lots and 1 of 27 patient sera (3.7%) positive, concluding that current US formulations are a rare cause. Formulations outside the US were not checked.

evidence.citation: Vergidis P, et al. J Clin Microbiol. 2014;52(6):2199-2201 (abstract)

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-invasive-mold-markers teaches the historical problem and its decline; the related simulator question carries a note.

flags.issue: Ch. 57 Hit 33 and simulator question 786 describe Aspergillus niger as having uniseriate phialides with smooth conidia. Samson 2007 lists A. niger among the biseriate species of section Nigri; the uniseriate black aspergilli are A. japonicus, A. aculeatus and relatives.

evidence.citation: Samson RA, et al. Diagnostic tools to identify black aspergilli. Stud Mycol. 2007;59:129-145

flags.appAction: Simulator question 786 carries a note; no lesson teaches the uniseriate claim.

flags.issue: Hit 10, Hit 15 and Trap 5 say anti-K titers underestimate fetal risk and call for MCA Doppler “regardless of titer.” A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis found that a maternal anti-K titer ≥ 8 had 97% sensitivity for severe HDFN needing intrauterine intervention, with 98.6% of severe cases at titers ≥ 8, and suggested guidelines be re-evaluated. Anti-K does suppress fetal erythropoiesis; guidance on critical titers differs.

evidence.citation: Jacobs JW, et al. Transfus Med Rev. 2025;39(2):150895
Valentini B, et al. Pregnancy (Hoboken). 2025;1(5):e70085

flags.appAction: Lesson ih-hdfn-titers-rhig teaches a lower anti-K critical titer with close surveillance and cites the 2025 meta-analysis; the related simulator question carries a note.

flags.issue: Simulator question 372 gives 2 vials for a 60 mL fetal whole-blood bleed (60 ÷ 30). Technical guidance cited by Hajjaj 2025 rounds the quotient (up if ≥ 0.5) and then adds one vial to cover maternal blood-volume and counting error, giving 3 vials; a Canadian survey shows practice varies.

evidence.citation: Hajjaj OI, et al. Br J Haematol. 2025;207(3):723-736

flags.appAction: Lesson ih-hdfn-titers-rhig teaches ÷ 30, round, plus one vial; simulator question 372 carries a note.

flags.issue: Hit 36 lists HACEK as the agents of “culture-negative subacute” endocarditis. HACEK organisms are slow-growing and CO₂-enhanced, but an automated blood-culture system detected ~99% within the standard 5 days, and prolonged incubation added no value (as summarized by Khaledi 2022).

evidence.citation: Khaledi M, et al. J Cardiothorac Surg. 2022;17(1):185

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-gn-oxidase-fastidious teaches CO₂ enhancement and ~99% detection within 5 days.

flags.issue: Hit 14 and Trap 6 say to keep platelets > 20 × 10⁹/L in bleeding DIC. The BCSH, JSTH and SISET guidelines and their ISTH harmonization, as summarized by Wada 2014, transfuse platelets in bleeding DIC at ≤ 50 × 10⁹/L and use 10–20 × 10⁹/L only for non-bleeding patients (e.g., after chemotherapy).

evidence.citation: Wada H, Matsumoto T, Yamashita Y. J Intensive Care. 2014;2(1):15

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-dic-liver-fibrinolysis teaches ≤ 50 × 10⁹/L for bleeding DIC.

flags.issue: Hit 3 and Trap 3 state that high insulin + high C-peptide = insulinoma. Sulfonylurea (and meglitinide) ingestion produces the same endogenous pattern; ENETS 2012 lists a negative sulfonylurea screen among the diagnostic criteria, and Peltola 2018 notes a negative oral hypoglycemic agent screen is needed to establish endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.

evidence.citation: Jensen RT, et al. Neuroendocrinology. 2012;95(2):98-119
Peltola E, et al. Int J Endocrinol. 2018;2018:2059481

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-ketones-hypoglycemia teaches the sulfonylurea screen.

flags.issue: Hit 8 says plerixafor is FDA-approved for NHL/multiple myeloma patients “failing G-CSF mobilization.” De Clercq 2019 describes the December 2008 FDA approval for autologous mobilization in NHL or multiple myeloma, given with G-CSF; rescue after poor mobilization is one use, not the approved population. The FDA label itself was not read.

evidence.citation: De Clercq E. Antivir Chem Chemother. 2019;27:2040206619829382

flags.appAction: Lesson ih-hpc-mobilization-ecp teaches the approval population and use with G-CSF.

flags.issue: Hit 5 defines septic arthritis as synovial WBC 50,000–200,000/µL with > 90% PMNs, low glucose and a positive Gram stain/culture. Long 2019 notes counts ≥ 50,000/µL also occur in gout and pseudogout, nearly half of culture-proven septic joints have ≤ 28,000/µL, synovial protein and glucose do not meaningfully change the likelihood, and Gram stain sensitivity is only ~29–65% for gram-positive infection.

evidence.citation: Long B, Koyfman A, Gottlieb M. West J Emerg Med. 2019;20(2):331-341

flags.appAction: Lesson cm-csf-synovial-interpretation teaches the overlap and that crystals and counts do not exclude infection.

flags.issue: Hit 4 (and Table 1) classes HTT 36–39 CAG repeats as “intermediate”. Nopoulos 2016 and Chintalaphani 2021 classify 36–39 as reduced (incomplete/partial) penetrance — some carriers develop Huntington disease — while 27–35 is the range that causes no disease but may expand on transmission.

evidence.citation: Nopoulos PC. Dialogues Clin Neurosci. 2016;18(1):91-98
Chintalaphani SR, et al. Acta Neuropathol Commun. 2021;9(1):98

flags.appAction: Lesson mdx-repeat-expansions teaches 27–35 intermediate, 36–39 reduced penetrance, ≥ 40 full penetrance.

flags.issue: Hit 5 says congenital myotonic dystrophy type 1 (1000–2000 CTG) is transmitted “MATERNALLY only”. Wenninger 2018: congenital DM1 expansions (> 800, usually ~1,000) are characteristically maternal, but congenital DM1 with paternal transmission is also known. Wenninger also gives 5–37 as healthy and > 50 as fully penetrant, not the reviewer’s 5–35 and > 100.

evidence.citation: Wenninger S, Montagnese F, Schoser B. Front Neurol. 2018;9:303

flags.appAction: Lesson mdx-repeat-expansions teaches “characteristically maternal; paternal cases are known”.

flags.issue: Hit 40 says to detect Shiga toxin directly in stool by EIA (or NAAT). Humphries & Linscott 2015 and CDC 2009 recommend Shiga toxin immunoassays on overnight enrichment broth (or primary-plate growth); direct-stool EIA has much lower sensitivity (~70%). NAAT for stx genes and simultaneous O157 culture remain appropriate (IDSA 2017).

evidence.citation: Humphries RM, Linscott AJ. Clin Microbiol Rev. 2015;28(1):3-31
Gould LH, et al. MMWR Recomm Rep. 2009;58(RR-12):1-14

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-enteric-pathogens-stec teaches broth-enriched EIA or stx NAAT, with simultaneous O157 culture.

flags.issue: Hit 14 says p24 antigen is the earliest detectable HIV marker. CDC 2014: HIV-1 RNA becomes detectable by NAT about 10 days after infection, and p24 antigen becomes detectable by 4th-generation assays 4–10 days after RNA. p24 precedes antibodies but is not the earliest marker.

evidence.citation: CDC/APHL. Laboratory Testing for the Diagnosis of HIV Infection: Updated Recommendations. 2014

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-hiv-hcv-testing-algorithms teaches RNA → p24 → antibody.

flags.issue: Hit 4 uses 4.4 g/dL as the reference albumin in the corrected-calcium formula (Ca + 0.8 × (4.4 − albumin)), and the simulator calls 4.0 g/dL “outdated”. Desgagnés 2025 and Mirrakhimov 2015 give the commonly used simplified Payne formula with 4.0 g/dL (40 g/L). Desgagnés 2025 also found unadjusted total calcium agreed with ionized calcium at least as well as adjusted calcium.

evidence.citation: Desgagnés N, et al. JAMA Netw Open. 2025;8(1):e2455251
Mirrakhimov AE. N Am J Med Sci. 2015;7(11):483-493

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-hypercalcemia-pth-pthrp teaches the 4.0 g/dL simplified Payne formula and its limits; local formulas may differ.

flags.issue: Hit 2 (and the Number Vault and memory section) states “MR2 = 10%” and describes each deep response as ~1.5 logs deeper. ELN 2020: 1%, 0.1%, 0.01%, 0.0032% and 0.001% IS correspond to 2, 3, 4, 4.5 and 5 logs below baseline, with MR³ (MMR), MR⁴ and MR⁴·⁵ named by their log reduction — so MR² corresponds to 1% IS; 10% is a 1-log reduction.

evidence.citation: Hochhaus A, et al. Leukemia. 2020;34(4):966-984

flags.appAction: Lesson mdx-cml-bcr-abl1-international-scale teaches the ELN log ladder.

flags.issue: Hit 1 (and Figure 76, Memory Hooks, Number Vault) gives oncoprotein assays a blanket 95–100% specificity, so that a positive “strongly implies malignancy”. Specificity is marker- and setting-specific: the NMP22 BladderChek test, listed in the same chapter, had pooled specificity 88% (sensitivity 56%) in a 19-study meta-analysis, and cystoscopy remains the gold standard.

evidence.citation: Wang Z, et al. Oncotarget. 2017;8(59):100648-100656

flags.appAction: Lesson mdx-oncoproteins-ras-p53-markers teaches NMP22’s pooled accuracy and that positives need cystoscopy.

flags.issue: Hit 4 (and the Number Vault) states KRAS mutations in “~75% of colon cancers”. Simanshu 2017 Table 1 gives KRAS 42% for colon (pancreas 91%, consistent with the reviewer’s >90%). Frequencies vary by study, but ~75% is well above this tabulation.

evidence.citation: Simanshu DK, Nissley DV, McCormick F. Cell. 2017;170(1):17-33

flags.appAction: Lesson mdx-oncoproteins-ras-p53-markers teaches the Simanshu Table 1 frequencies.

flags.issue: Hit 7 and Trap 2 state that ACE inhibition “is a risk factor for cognitive impairment/AD onset”. A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis (18 studies) found lower dementia risk with Ang-II stimulating antihypertensives than with Ang-II inhibiting ones (a class that includes ACE inhibitors) in observational studies, but the meta-analysis of RCTs was non-significant. A causal risk from ACE inhibitors is not established; the statement is presented as settled.

evidence.citation: Belachew EA, Peterson GM, Bezabhe WM. Geroscience. 2025;47(4):5525-5541

flags.appAction: Not taught as fact; lesson mdx-apoe-alzheimer-amyloid carries the flag.

flags.issue: Hit 4 states that any positive direct CDC crossmatch with current recipient serum is an “absolute contraindication” to renal transplantation. Althaf 2017 grades positive crossmatches by antibody class and specificity: IgG HLA donor-specific antibody is the veto, but CDC positives that disappear with DTT (IgM, often autoreactive non-HLA) are standard risk, and lupus immune complexes can give false-positive B-cell CDC results (worked case: FCXM negative, no DSA on single-antigen beads).

evidence.citation: Althaf MM, et al. World J Transplant. 2017;7(6):339-348

flags.appAction: Lesson immuno-hla-crossmatch-pra teaches DTT, FCXM and single-antigen-bead resolution of positive crossmatches.

flags.issue: Hit 6 states CVID diagnosis requires “age >2 years”. That is the 1999 ESID/PAGID definition. The 2016 International Consensus Document (ICON) advises that, because of the broad differential and the difficulty of assessing vaccine responses in early childhood, CVID is best not diagnosed before at least age 4 years.

evidence.citation: Bonilla FA, et al. J Allergy Clin Immunol Pract. 2016;4(1):38-59

flags.appAction: Lesson immuno-pid-trec-dhr-cvid teaches both definitions and the ICON age advice.

flags.issue: Hit 1 presents anti-endomysial antibody (anti-EMA) as the confirmation test (“nearly 100% specific for confirmation”). The ESsCD 2025 adult guideline states that routine IgA anti-EMA serology is no longer recommended for confirmation; adults are confirmed by duodenal biopsy or, conditionally, without biopsy if under 45 years with IgA anti-TG2 ≥ 10 × ULN confirmed in a second sample.

evidence.citation: Al-Toma A, et al. United European Gastroenterol J. 2025;13(10):1855-1886

flags.appAction: Lesson immuno-celiac-serology-pbc-ama teaches the 2025 confirmation pathway.

flags.issue: Hit 11 states “relative risk RR = (a×d)/(b×c)”. That cross-product ratio is the odds ratio, the measure used for HLA–disease association in case-control studies (Ziade 2017 calculates the OR with the classic formula a*d/b*c). It is not a risk ratio.

evidence.citation: Ziade NR. BMC Musculoskelet Disord. 2017;18(1):280

flags.appAction: Lesson immuno-hla-disease-association teaches the formula as the odds ratio.

flags.issue: Hit 6 gives HFE C282Y homozygote penetrance “as low as 1–10%”. Penetrance depends on how disease is defined; in the eMERGE network the clinical diagnostic rate of haemochromatosis among C282Y homozygotes was 24.4% in males and 14.0% in females. The reviewer’s point (most homozygotes never develop disease; no population screening) is consistent, but the figure should be qualified.

evidence.citation: Gallego CJ, et al. Am J Hum Genet. 2015;97(4):512-520

flags.appAction: Lesson immuno-hla-disease-association teaches the eMERGE figures.

flags.issue: Hit 2 (and the matching Memory Hook and 5-Second Recall) defines Isolation as “concurrent transactions behave as sequential”. That describes only the strictest (serializable) isolation level; databases offer weaker levels and often default to one (PostgreSQL defaults to Read Committed). The general definition is that a transaction’s effects are not visible to concurrent transactions before it commits.

evidence.citation: PostgreSQL Documentation (current): Glossary; Section 13.2 Transaction Isolation

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-lis-audit-trail-ngs-files teaches the general definition and notes that isolation has levels.

flags.issue: Hit 3, the Number Vault and the 5-Second Recall define contribution margin as price minus FULLY LOADED cost (PSA example: $41.54 − $34.62 = $6.92). Standard managerial accounting defines contribution margin as selling price minus VARIABLE cost per unit (its contribution toward fixed costs, then profit); price minus fully loaded cost is profit per unit. The reviewer may follow its source text’s usage, but candidates should know the standard definition.

evidence.citation: Franklin M, Graybeal P, Cooper D. Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting. OpenStax; 2019. Section 3.1

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-test-cost-breakeven-npv teaches the standard definition and points to this flag.

flags.issue: Trap 4 says a positive NPV is not enough and that IRR must also be checked against the cost of capital. Because IRR is the discount rate at which NPV = 0, for a conventional project (one outlay followed by inflows) a positive NPV at the cost of capital already means IRR exceeds that rate; the two tests agree on accept/reject. They can conflict only when ranking mutually exclusive projects or with unconventional cash flows. The reviewer’s own example (negative NPV, IRR 8% < 10%) is consistent.

evidence.citation: Franklin M, Graybeal P, Cooper D. Principles of Accounting, Volume 2: Managerial Accounting. OpenStax; 2019. Section 11.4

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-test-cost-breakeven-npv states that NPV > 0 and IRR > required rate are the same test for a conventional project.

flags.issue: Hit 3 and Trap 2 state that the IRB, not the investigator, decides exemption. The Common Rule text (45 CFR 46.104) lists exempt categories but does not say who makes the determination; that is set by institutional policy, and OHRP guidance (which the app could not fetch, HTTP 403) is commonly cited as recommending that investigators not decide alone. Many institutions assign it to the IRB office, but “the IRB, never the investigator” is a policy norm, not a regulatory requirement as far as the regulation text shows.

flags.issue: States that oxacillin susceptibility 'only rules out mecA'. Paterson 2014 reports that on the Vitek 2 system most mecC MRSA are cefoxitin-resistant but oxacillin-susceptible (other automated systems not fully tested), and that cefoxitin is more reliable than oxacillin in disc diffusion, broth microdilution and agar dilution. flags.issue: Hit 9 says Southern and northern blots are 'both largely replaced by amplification methods'. Open sources qualify this. Yang 2022 says northern blotting is still used as a gold standard for validating high-throughput expression data and uniquely gives transcript size and expression level, although qPCR is now often used. Pandelache 2021 reports a Southern blot detecting fragile X full-mutation alleles that two PCR assays missed: AmplideX triplet-primed PCR and long-range methylation-sensitive PCR. flags.issue: Hit 4 presents type 3 dysbetalipoproteinemia as an 'equal cholesterol and TG elevation' with tuberoeruptive xanthomas, which reads as a pattern you can recognise from a standard panel. Heidemann 2022: FD is usually a mixed hyperlipidemia but can present as predominant hypertriglyceridemia or hypercholesterolemia; the standard lipid panel cannot detect the phenotype (ultracentrifugation VLDL-C/total TG >0.30 by mass, or apoB-based methods, are needed, plus a causal APOE genotype for a formal diagnosis); about 90% of cases are e2e2, but only 10-15% of e2e2 people express the phenotype (Pallazola 2020 gives fewer than 5%); the broad-beta band is highly specific but has low sensitivity. Pallazola 2020: HLP3 cannot be diagnosed from the standard lipid profile. Sampson 2022: striate palmar xanthomas are considered pathognomonic, while tubero-eruptive xanthomas also occur in other dyslipidemias.

flags.issue: The reviewer says an ESR >100 mm/h in a known cancer patient usually means metastases. Abbag 2007 says that in adults, solid tumours causing an ESR >=100 mm/h are often (not usually) associated with metastasis. It also reports infection as the most common cause of ESR >=100 in paediatric and adult series, with malignancy third. Sensitivity of ESR >=100 for malignancy is low: 0.25 in the 1006-patient series summarised by Markanday 2015 and 25-49% per Abbag 2007. Markanday also reports specificity of 0.96 for malignancy and an identifiable cause in 90%. So an extreme ESR in a cancer patient, especially one with fever, needs a search for infection and cannot be read as metastasis by default.

evidence.citation: Abbag FI, Al Qahtani JM. Ann Saudi Med. 2007;27(3):175-178
Markanday A. Open Forum Infect Dis. 2015;2(3):ofv098

flags.issue: The reviewer says temporal arteritis/polymyalgia rheumatica typically run >90 mm/h. No open source read supports a typical >90 mm/h value. Manzo 2018 reports that 7-22% of PMR patients have a normal ESR at diagnosis, usually with a raised CRP, and that biopsy-proven GCA can occur with a normal ESR and CRP. In Kermani 2012 (abstract read; full text not open access), an elevated ESR had a sensitivity of 84.1% for a positive temporal artery biopsy, and 4% of biopsy-positive GCA patients had both ESR and CRP normal.

Kermani TA, et al. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 2012;41(6):866-871

flags.issue: Trap 4 says functional tests (erythrocyte Cu-Zn superoxide dismutase activity) are more meaningful than serum copper. The one study read was in rats. In it, erythrocyte and liver SOD1 activity did not fall significantly in mild zinc-induced copper deficiency (they fell only on a frankly copper-deficient diet), while copper chaperone for SOD1 (CCS) did fall. The authors note that no gold standard exists. The trap's point that serum copper and ceruloplasmin are confounded and thought to miss marginal deficiency is supported.

flags.issue: Trap 6 says plasma is preferred, and the Number Vault trick says serum runs 5-10% higher than plasma. The BOND zinc review reports that early studies found serum zinc slightly higher than plasma, put this down to serum samples standing longer before separation, and found no difference when both were held equally long. BOND's suggested lower plasma zinc cut-offs also differ by fasting state, time of day and sex (µg/dL): morning fasting 70 F / 74 M; morning non-fasting 66 F / 70 M; afternoon 59 F / 61 M. The trap's points on diurnal variation and haemolysis (blood cells hold about 10 times plasma zinc) are supported.

evidence.citation: King JC, et al. J Nutr. 2015;146(4):858S-885S

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-zinc-copper-status-menkes teaches timing-specific BOND cut-offs, haemolysis and collection precautions, and that serum and plasma zinc did not differ when handled alike.

flags.issue: Hit 46 says 16S rRNA sequencing 'gives a definitive bacterial ID'. Janda 2007 reports genus-level identification in most cases (>90%) but species-level identification less often (65-83%), poor discrimination for some groups (two Bacillus type strains >99.5% similar; Enterobacter/Pantoea; Streptococcus mitis group), and warns that the closest database match cannot always be taken as a definitive identification. Church 2020 states that the 16S target alone may not reliably identify many human pathogens and cannot differentiate species within the M. tuberculosis complex. 16S is an appropriate next step for an unidentifiable isolate, but the result is not always definitive at species level.

flags.issue: Hit 15 (and Exam Trap 5) says SDS-PAGE separates proteins by molecular mass 'alone'. Estimating MW this way assumes every protein binds a consistent amount of SDS. Full-length membrane proteins show gel shifts of about -46% to +48% from their formula MW, and in model membrane hairpins the shifts tracked altered SDS loading. Highly acidic proteins can appear larger than their predicted MW, and glycosylation can slow migration. Mass-based separation is still the correct principle, but 'alone' needs this caveat.

evidence.citation: Rath A, et al. Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. 2009;106(6):1760-1765

flags.issue: Hit 17's 'large molecules elute first' is correct as the ideal rule. But SEC separates by size in solution (Stokes radius), which does not track molecular weight exactly because proteins differ in shape. Interactions with the packing can also shift elution: ion exclusion makes a protein elute earlier than predicted, and ionic adsorption or hydrophobic interaction makes it elute later.

evidence.citation: Hong P, et al. J Liq Chromatogr Relat Technol. 2012;35(20):2923-2950

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-protein-separation-sec-sds-ief teaches large-first elution with the Stokes-radius and secondary-interaction caveats (accuracy flag f-sec-stokes).

flags.issue: Hit 11 says the MS workup uses 'IFE' on unconcentrated CSF paired with serum, without naming isoelectric focusing. The open sources describe the reference method as isoelectric focusing (IEF) followed by IgG-specific immunoblotting or immunofixation, with CSF and serum run in parallel at equal IgG. flags.issue: Hit 4, Exam Trap 1, the Do-not-confuse table (Table 2) and its closing line call up-coding and unbundling 'illegal fraud' with no qualification. The OIG laboratory compliance guidance says intentional or knowing upcoding 'could violate the False Claims Act and/or other civil laws, and criminal law'. The False Claims Act makes a person liable for knowingly presenting a false or fraudulent claim. It defines 'knowingly' to include deliberate ignorance and reckless disregard, and requires no proof of specific intent to defraud. The CMS NCCI manual treats unbundling and upcoding as improper coding that providers must avoid, and says NCCI was developed to prevent inappropriate payment. In these sources, fraud liability depends on knowing conduct; they do not treat every coding error as fraud.

flags.issue: Trap 6 (and Hit 9) say the lab must give the patient an ABN before the test if Medicare may deny it. That is right as far as it goes, but it leaves out conditions in the CMS ABN form instructions and the OIG laboratory guidance. CMS: deliver the ABN before the service, far enough in advance for an informed choice; review it with the patient; give a reason for each listed test; keep a signed copy; ABNs are never required in emergencies. OIG: the notice must be written, identify the particular service, state that payment is likely to be denied and give the reason. Patients should not be asked to sign blank ABNs. Routine notices that only say denial is possible, or notices given for all services, are not acceptable. The OIG also notes that labs often find it hard to obtain ABNs directly and may educate ordering physicians on their use.

flags.issue: Hit 12 instructs treating all SPACE organisms (Serratia, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Citrobacter, Enterobacter) as resistant to extended-spectrum cephalosporins except cefepime. The ARLG AmpC primer names Enterobacter spp. (and K. aerogenes) as the most problematic for AmpC induction, reports that derepressed Serratia marcescens, Morganella morganii and Providencia stuartii express about ten-fold less AmpC than derepressed Enterobacter cloacae or Citrobacter freundii, states that because AmpC production is less prominent for the other 'SPACE' organisms it is reasonable to base treatment decisions on in vitro susceptibility results, and classes Acinetobacter baumannii chromosomal resistance as noninducible. It lists P. aeruginosa as having inducible chromosomal ampC but limits its treatment discussion to Enterobacteriaceae. It also states that observational data support both cefepime (preferentially every 8 hours) and piperacillin-tazobactam as acceptable, that the question is largely unsettled, and that carbapenem superiority is unproven.

flags.issue: Hit 42 says never to culture a surface swab of an open wound. CODIFI (400 patients with suspected infected diabetic foot ulcer, England) found that a Levine-technique wound swab, taken after cleansing and debridement, still reported at least one potential pathogen in 70.1% of patients versus 86.1% for tissue (curette or scalpel). Pathogen results differed in 58% of patients, with more pathogens and fewer contaminants from tissue. Tissue collection caused more ulcer pain (9.3% vs 1.3%) and bleeding (6.8% vs 1.5%). The preference for tissue is therefore method- and collection-technique dependent rather than absolute. No open source read supports the aspirate option or the site-by-site pathogen map in the same item.

flags.issue: Hit 10 frames unrelated HCT matching as '10 of 10' (A, B, C, DRB1, DQB1) and says HLA-A mismatches have the largest impact on GVHD and survival. It reports that any single mismatch at these loci was associated with worse overall survival, with no evidence that mismatch at any one locus was better tolerated. It states that DQB1 has not been shown in isolation to substantially affect survival, and it recommends DPB1 typing with matched or permissive T-cell-epitope mismatches.

flags.issue: Hit 14 states normal B cells express kappa OR lambda light chains, 'never both', and that light-chain restriction proves clonality. Pauza et al. (abstract) found normal human fetal marrow and spleen B cells co-expressing surface kappa and lambda at 2-3% of surface-Ig+ B cells and state this refutes the concept that single light-chain isotype expression is immutable. Guillory et al. describe hematogones with lambda light-chain restriction by flow but no clonal IG heavy or kappa rearrangement by PCR, so flow restriction does not always prove clonality. Restriction remains a valid population-level sign of a clone (reactive kappa:lambda about 1.5:1 per Gajzer & Fromm 2025), but 'never' and 'proves' are too absolute.

flags.issue: Hit 6 says 'CLL/SLL needs >=5,000 monoclonal B cells/μL' and that below that a CLL-phenotype clone is MBL. WHO-HAEM5 requires no other features diagnostic of CLL/SLL, separates low-count MBL (<0.5 x 10^9/L) from CLL/SLL-type MBL (>=0.5 x 10^9/L), and states the upper limit as a total B-cell count <5 x 10^9/L. A count below 5,000/μL alone therefore does not exclude CLL/SLL. SLL in particular is diagnosed without the leukaemic count, on lymphadenopathy and/or splenomegaly with lymph node biopsy (Chiattone 2025), so the 5,000/μL requirement applies to CLL, not SLL.

flags.issue: Hit 11 says iodine excess shuts down synthesis '(hypothyroidism)' and 'iodine deficiency → Jod-Basedow phenomenon (hyperthyroidism)'. Leung and Braverman 2014 describe Jod-Basedow as iodine-induced hyperthyroidism, which follows an iodine LOAD. Its risk factors are nontoxic or diffuse nodular goitre, latent Graves disease and long-standing iodine deficiency, so deficiency is a risk factor rather than the trigger. They also describe the Wolff–Chaikoff reduction in hormone synthesis as transient (about 24 h in rats), with escape through decreased sodium–iodide symporter expression. Hypothyroidism develops in susceptible patients who fail to escape, for example those with autoimmune thyroid disease or previously treated Graves disease.

evidence.citation: Leung AM, Braverman LE. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2014;10(3):136-142

flags.issue: Hit 3 presents TSH as the first-line thyroid test without its limits. Koulouri 2013 (Table 1) lists conditions in which TSH alone may mislead: recent treatment for thyrotoxicosis (TSH may stay suppressed), non-thyroidal illness, TSH assay interference, central hypothyroidism, TSH-secreting adenoma, resistance to thyroid hormone, and disorders of thyroid hormone transport or metabolism. The same paper notes that many laboratories now combine TSH with T4. The 2018 ETA guideline states that diagnostic accuracy improves when both TSH and free T4 are measured.

evidence.citation: Koulouri O, et al. Best Pract Res Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2013;27(6):745-762
Kahaly GJ, et al. Eur Thyroid J. 2018;7(4):167-186

flags.issue: Hit 11 and Exam Trap 3 (also Memory Hook and Number Vault) set the PT investigation threshold at more than about 2.5 SDI, with a 0.6% chance of being a true inlier. Kristensen and Meijer 2017 cite ISO/IEC 17043:2010: |z| up to 2 is satisfactory, between 2 and 3 is questionable (a warning signal that should be investigated), and 3 or more is unsatisfactory (an action signal). KEQAS treats SDI above 3 as unacceptable. Coucke and Soumali 2017 give 4.6% and 0.27% beyond |z| of 2 and 3 under normality. 0.6% is the one-tailed normal tail beyond 2.5 SD; the two-sided figure is about 1.2%. Cut-offs depend on the scheme. The advice to investigate a passing result still holds, but the 2.5 threshold and the 0.6% figure are not a general standard.

evidence.citation: Kristensen GB, Meijer P. Biochem Med (Zagreb). 2017;27(1):49-62
Coucke W, Soumali MR. Biochem Med (Zagreb). 2017;27(1):37-48
Kim S, et al. Ann Lab Med. 2021;41(2):230-239

flags.issue: Hit 3 and Exam Trap 1 (also the Memory Hook and 5-Second Recall) say that after a reagent lot change you adjust the QC target and never the SD. Thompson and Chesher 2018 say that when patient data show no clinically significant difference, the new lot can still show IQC changes in the running mean or SD, and the IQC targets can safely be altered. ICSH 2024 says IQC values (targets and limits) should be assessed for new coagulation reagent lots. For a new lot of unassayed control material, ICSH accepts limits from either a recalculated mean plus or minus 2 SD or the mean plus or minus 2 times the previously determined SD. The sources read do not support an absolute ban on changing the SD; whether to keep the established SD looks like a laboratory policy choice. CLSI C24 was not read.

Gosselin RC, et al. Semin Thromb Hemost. 2024;50(8):1091-1102

The claim that lithium is the only mood stabilizer thoroughly examined pharmacogenomically was not verified by any source read.

flags.issue: Hit 6 (repeated in Exam Trap 2) says significance can 'always' be forced or manufactured by inflating n. So a large n makes tiny non-zero effects significant; it does not manufacture significance for a true null.

flags.issue: Hit 7 (and Exam Trap 3) presents the Bonferroni correction as the remedy for multiple comparisons without caveats. Ranganathan 2016 says Bonferroni has been criticised as far too conservative, especially for highly correlated tests, that alpha adjustment raises Type II (false-negative) risk, and lists Holm, Hochberg and false-discovery-rate (Benjamini-Hochberg) procedures. Andrade 2019 says Bonferroni magnifies Type II risk, that the Hochberg procedure balances the two errors better, that correction mainly applies to many tests of the same construct, and that it may be dispensed with in exploratory studies.

flags.issue: Hit 17 equates low CSF glucose + high protein + neutrophilic pleocytosis with bacterial meningitis without noting that the pattern is often incomplete. flags.issue: Hit 8 says Perls grades marrow storage iron 0–5+ with normal adult 2+, as if this were a single standard scale. flags.issue: Hit 7 (and Exam Trap 3) names overfitting as the SELDI-TOF-MS pattern-diagnostics pitfall. Open sources add that discriminating peaks can come from non-biologic experimental bias, such as sample handling, storage and run differences. A re-analysis of a public ovarian SELDI dataset found the best-separating m/z values below 500, in a region often treated as noise, and concluded there was a non-biologic experimental bias between the cancer and control samples. Peak amplitudes may decline with repeated freeze-thaw cycles, and instrument drift can shift peak positions. A later study with stringent protocols and an independent validation cohort reached 73-81% accuracy for ovarian cancer versus benign tumours and judged SELDI-TOF-MS not applicable to routine patient care.

ABO-identical WBITs are likely to go undetected ('silent errors'). Electronic patient identification was associated with about fivefold fewer WBITs (rates cited by Obaidallah from Kaufman et al.), so bedside electronic identification is a prevention measure rather than a detection method.

flags.issue: Trap 3 lists low calcium/phosphate among osteomalacia labs. Hypocalcemia can occur (Schini 2023 lists it among the main features). However, in vitamin D or calcium deprivation, secondary hyperparathyroidism keeps serum calcium normal until compensation fails, so calcium is a poor marker and a normal calcium does not exclude osteomalacia (Uday & Hogler 2017). Raised ALP and PTH with low 25OHD is the typical biochemistry, and hypophosphataemia drives the mineralization defect. Osteomalacia can also lower BMD, so a low T-score does not exclude it.

flags.issue: Trap 6 says Paget disease typically shows normal calcium and phosphate with markedly elevated ALP (plus urinary hydroxyproline), and that hypercalcemia would point elsewhere. Total ALP with liver tests is the recommended first-line test, but total ALP can be normal: 42% of Paget cases in the Rotterdam cohort had normal total ALP, particularly monostotic forms. Bone ALP, PINP or uNTX may be considered when total ALP is normal and suspicion is high. Calcium homeostasis is usually maintained, but immobilization can cause hypercalcemia and hypercalciuria in Paget patients. Urinary hydroxyproline is an older, diet-affected, non-bone-specific marker and is not part of the current first-line recommendation.

flags.issue: The hit equates purulent sputum with no dominant routine-culture organism with atypical pneumonia. Absence of dominant growth is consistent with but does not establish an atypical pathogen: even with culture plus nucleic acid amplification a cause is established in no more than about half of pneumonia episodes, and clinical presentation alone does not accurately discriminate atypical from typical pneumonia. flags.issue: The reviewer says the positivity criterion chooses the cutoff whose LR+ best matches LR_threshold = [P(not D)/P(D)] x [(cTN - cFP)/(cTP - cFN)]. flags.issue: Hit 4 lists seven schizophrenia CNV hot spots. It does not say whether each is a deletion or a duplication, or how few cases carry them. Losses: 1q21.1, 2p16.3 (NRXN1), 3q29, 15q13.3, distal 16p11.2 and 22q11.2. Gains: 7q11.23 (7q11.2 in the abstract) and proximal 16p11.2. 1q21.1 is listed as both a loss and a gain. Together these loci are carried by only 1.4% of cases. The 22q11.21 deletion has the largest finite odds ratio (67.7); the 3q29 loss is listed as infinite.

The 1q21.1 (P=0.022) and 3q29 (P=0.03) results were only nominally significant, and the authors state that replication in independent studies is required. flags.issue: Hit 4 (and the Number Vault row) gives 80-95% photodeprotection efficiency per cycle, and so 1-36% correct 20-mers, as a general figure. Sack 2016 says the relatively low stepwise yield came from early MeNPOC/DMBOC photolabile groups and limited those arrays to short oligomers, and that NPPOC gives almost quantitative coupling. Agbavwe 2011 reports early MeNPOC coupling of 92-94% and measured average stepwise coupling of about 98.5-99% in maskless array synthesis. The same paper notes that the effective stepwise yield is lower than coupling efficiency, because incomplete photodeprotection and stray light also cause errors. Stepwise yield therefore depends on coupling and deprotection together, not on photodeprotection alone, and modern full-length fractions cannot be read straight off the coupling figure.

The sources do support the neutral backbone, the more stable PNA-DNA duplexes, insensitivity to ionic strength, the larger single-mismatch Tm penalty (~15 vs 4 °C) and resistance to enzymatic degradation.

flags.issue: Hit 4 (and the Memory Hook / 5-Second Recall) says MSI-H (>=2 of 5 markers) leads to a Lynch syndrome workup, but it never says MSI-H is only a screen. About 15% of colorectal cancers are MSI-H while Lynch causes about 3%. Current screening pipelines test MMR-deficient tumours for BRAF V600E and MLH1 promoter methylation, both linked to sporadic tumours, and send only tumours with neither for germline MMR testing. The mixed NCI five-marker panel (2 mononucleotide + 3 dinucleotide markers) also frequently misclassified MSH6-deficient tumours as MSS/MSI-L. Labs now use mononucleotide-only panels, and immunohistochemistry should stain all four MMR proteins.
