flags.issue: Hit 7 says central DI = urine osmolality rise >10% after desmopressin and nephrogenic DI = rise <10%. The classic (Miller) criteria summarised in open reviews use a >50% rise (with urine osmolality <300 mOsm/kg on thirsting) for complete central DI and call smaller rises nephrogenic; a >9% rise is used only to separate partial central DI from primary polydipsia when thirsted urine is 300-800 mOsm/kg. A 2024 review gives <15% for complete and up to 45% for partial nephrogenic DI. The Miller cut-offs were post hoc derived from a small cohort and the water deprivation test was only 77% accurate in a 156-patient study.

evidence.citation: Refardt J, Winzeler B, Christ-Crain M. Clin Endocrinol (Oxf). 2019;91(1):22-32
Flynn K, et al. Front Endocrinol (Lausanne). 2024;15:1479764

Baseline values in central DI and primary polydipsia overlap; only a baseline >21.4 pmol/L (nephrogenic DI) is diagnostic without stimulation. Sources also differ on the boundary value (Refardt 2019: >4.9 = primary polydipsia; Flynn 2024: >=4.9).

flags.issue: Hit 5 and the Number Vault rows give the Fourth UDMI (2018) procedural MI multiples as the definition: type 4a > 5x and type 5 > 10x the 99th percentile within 48 h, and reinfarction as a > 20% rise over 3-6 h. The Fifth UDMI (2026) defines procedure-related MI within 30 days of any cardiac procedure without relying on biomarker thresholds, using the same criteria for percutaneous and surgical procedures. Higher values that are still rising (e.g. > 5x URL at 6 h after intervention, > 35x at 24 h after surgery) make it likely. It is confirmed by an angiographic coronary complication or new imaging loss of viable myocardium, and both are required when the complication arose during the procedure or the procedure was done for acute MI. For recurrent MI it says rising serial values suggest recurrence. It mentions a < 20% change only as an imprecision-based sign of stable chronic injury. More specific than rv-udmi-fifth.

evidence.citation: Mills NL, et al. Glob Heart. 2026;21(1):64
Domienik-Karłowicz J, et al. Cardiol J. 2021;28(2):195-201

flags.issue: Hit 6 says unstable angina is 'managed like NSTEMI'. The Fifth UDMI notes that unstable angina without troponin elevation has a more favourable prognosis and is confirmed only when angiography shows an acute coronary pathology. Paiva 2024 says patients with unstable angina seem to have a lower risk of death and get less benefit from intensified antiplatelet therapy and early invasive strategies than patients with NSTEMI. It also says guidelines give no practical algorithm for unstable angina once MI is ruled out. Unstable angina stays within the ACS spectrum, but the claim that management is the same as for NSTEMI needs checking against current ACS guidelines.

evidence.citation: Mills NL, et al. Glob Heart. 2026;21(1):64
Paiva L, et al. Glob Heart. 2024;19(1):7

flags.issue: Hit 12 (and the 'Five per cell' Memory Hook, the Number Vault 'Chi-square validity floor' row and the 5-Second Recall answer) says chi-square is valid only if every cell has ≥5 expected observations. flags.issue: Hit 13 says paired t-tests are more powerful than unpaired. Kim 2015 shows Var(A−B) = σ1² + σ2² − 2ρσ1σ2: the paired test gains power only when the paired values are positively correlated and loses power when they are negatively correlated; Kim 2015 also warns that using an independent t-test on such paired data gives incorrect results.

evidence.citation: Kim TK. Korean J Anesthesiol. 2015;68(6):540-546

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-paired-chi-square-rank-tests teaches the power gain as conditional on positive correlation (accuracy flag f-paired-power-correlation).

flags.issue: Trap 6 says to switch to rank-based tests when a parametric test meets 'wildly non-Gaussian data', without trade-offs. Ghasemi 2012 notes that with large enough samples (>30 or 40) violation of normality should not cause major problems for parametric procedures, and Nahm 2016 notes rank tests can have lower power ('always valid, but not always efficient') and recommends parametric methods when they can be used.

flags.issue: Hit 6 (and Exam Trap 3) state that one case report is not research but a second case is a systematic investigation requiring IRB review. The US regulations do not define how many cases make research; most IRBs locally define both the number of cases that are not human subjects research and the threshold at which systematic investigation is reached, and institutional practice varies (some require formal IRB exemption letters even for a single case report, others leave it to authors or department heads). 'Second case = research' is one local convention, not a federal rule.

evidence.citation: Bass PF, Maloy JW. Ochsner J. 2020;20(1):56-61
Valešić M, Čivljak M, Puljak L. BMC Med Ethics. 2025;26(1):64

flags.issue: Trap 2 (and Hit 3) describe exempt studies as using deidentified, already-collected data. 45 CFR 46.104(d)(4) also exempts secondary research on identifiable private information that is publicly available, or whose use is regulated under HIPAA for health care operations, research or public health activities; conversely, data that are not identifiable to the investigator may fall outside the 46.102(e) human-subject definition altogether. 'Exempt = deidentified' is an oversimplification.

Deidentified data may therefore still be re-linkable by the holder of the code.

flags.issue: Exam Trap 3 and the 'Do not confuse' table (Trap 7 / Table 2) call likelihood ratios 'prevalence-proof' and sensitivity/specificity 'No — test properties'. That holds arithmetically when sensitivity and specificity are fixed, but in practice estimates vary between populations: across 23 meta-analyses, sensitivity, specificity or both were significantly associated with prevalence in 8 (35%), with higher prevalence accompanying lower specificity in all 8, and in one pulmonary embolism review LR+ ranged from 2.35 to 25.4 across studies. Patient spectrum and referral filters are proposed mechanisms; the authors do not claim prevalence itself is the cause. (High-Yield Hit 5 and the 'prevalence-proof' Memory Hook repeat the same wording.)

flags.issue: Hit 13 states that septic-shock survival drops 7.6% per hour of delay in effective antibiotics, with no context. The figure is an average over the first 6 h after onset of septic-shock hypotension in one major retrospective analysis (Kumar 2006, as summarised by its first author in 2014). The 2021 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline notes that the time-to-antibiotics studies are observational and at risk of bias, and that the association is strong in septic shock but weaker and less consistent without shock. It recommends antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 h of recognition, for possible septic shock or a high likelihood of sepsis, and within 3 h for possible sepsis without shock if concern for infection persists. The number should not be extrapolated linearly or causally beyond that setting.

evidence.citation: Kumar A. Virulence. 2014;5(1):80-97
Evans L, et al. Intensive Care Med. 2021;47(11):1181-1247

flags.appAction: Lesson micro-antibiotic-targets-synergy-sepsis-clock teaches the 7.6% figure with its setting (septic shock, first 6 h after hypotension, retrospective) and the SSC 2021 timing recommendations.

flags.issue: Hit 14 presents synergy thresholds as fixed. Doern 2014 defines time-kill synergy as a >2 log10 (not ≥2) increase in kill by the combination over its most active constituent, best assessed in the first 12 h. It states that there is no true gold standard for synergy, that no two synergy methods produce comparable results, and that synergy testing cannot be recommended for routine use to guide patient care. Other studies use different FICI cutoffs: Stein 2015 used FICI <0.8 for synergy and ≥4 for antagonism, based on median FICI. The thresholds are therefore method-dependent.

evidence.citation: Doern CD. J Clin Microbiol. 2014;52(12):4124-4128
Stein C, et al. PLoS One. 2015;10(6):e0126479

flags.issue: Hit 9 gives AChR antibodies in 85-90% of myasthenia gravis, anti-MuSK in 30-40% of the remainder and about 5% double-negative. The MuSK fraction agrees with Lazaridis and Tzartos 2020 (MuSK in about 6% of all MG, accounting for 40% of patients without AChR antibodies), but the two reviews put AChR at about 85% (80-85% by radioimmunoprecipitation) and the seronegative fraction at about 10%, not about 5%, on the classical AChR and MuSK assays, with cell-based or improved immunoprecipitation assays detecting antibodies in some of those patients. The hit also omits that AChR sensitivity is about 85% in generalised but only about 50% in ocular myasthenia gravis, and that MuSK is less common in Japanese patients (2-3%). Frequencies depend on assay and population.

flags.issue: Hit 14 states atrophic thyroiditis is TSI-negative. Diana, Olivo and Kahaly 2018 report that 19 of 24 (79%) TBAb-positive patients with atrophic thyroiditis remained hypothyroid but that 2 of 34 TBAb-positive hypothyroid patients went on to develop TSAb-positive Graves hyperthyroidism, Furmaniak 2013 showed stimulating and blocking TSH receptor antibodies can be produced by one patient's B cells at the same time, and Vargas-Uricoechea 2023 describes TBAb together with TSAb in patients with alternating hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism with atrophic thyroiditis. TSI negativity in atrophic thyroiditis is therefore a usual pattern rather than an absolute rule.

flags.issue: Hit 10 (and Exam Trap 4, plus the chapter's '14-day insulin amnesia' memory hook) sets the limit at more than 14 days of insulin therapy. The 2023 laboratory guideline states that insulin treatment precludes the analysis of insulin autoantibodies because it takes only about 11 days before insulin antibodies are induced, and Kawasaki 2023 counted insulin autoantibodies as positive only in insulin-naive patients or those within 2 weeks of starting insulin. A fixed 14-day window is therefore more permissive than the guideline, and the safe rule is to draw the sample before insulin starts.

flags.issue: Trap 2 calls Light's criteria the validated discriminator for pericardial fluid. flags.issue: Hit 13 gives a typical serum MBL of 1.5 ug/mL and MBL deficiency in ~5% of the population. Level-based prevalence depends on the cut-off (studies use 100, 500 or 1000 ng/mL) and more than 10% of the general population may be classified deficient depending on definition (Thiel 2006). Levels range from about 5 ng/mL to more than 10 ug/mL (Thiel 2006), healthy adults usually exceed 1000 ng/mL (Auriti 2017), and levels can rise during inflammation (3-4-fold per Auriti 2017; a small acute-phase increase per Thiel 2006). flags.issue: Trap 4 says to check the pulse: racing points to volume loss, crashing points to vagal. Sources confirm the opposite autonomic signatures, but presyncope signs reflect both sympathetic and parasympathetic activation (sinus tachycardia is noted if the donor is standing), and in a large donor study the vascular response, not the parasympathetic slowing of heart rate, was described as the main cause of the faint. In an apheresis series both reactions are first managed the same way (pause, start a fluid infusion), and response to fluid helps separate them. The pulse is a clue, not proof.

evidence.citation: Basavarajegowda A, Nalini YC. Asian J Transfus Sci. 2024;18(2):296-302
Philip J, Sarkar RS, Jain N. Asian J Transfus Sci. 2014;8(1):43-46
Philip J, Sarkar RS, Pathak A. Asian J Transfus Sci. 2013;7(1):37-41

flags.appAction: Lesson bb-donor-blood-volume-reactions-draw-time teaches the autonomic fork as a clue and adds response to fluid as a second discriminator.

flags.issue: The reviewer calls the purest grade 'Type I' water and attributes resistivity > 10 MΩ·cm to CLSI/CAP. The CLSI GP40 (5th ed., 2024) product description lists water types by use (clinical laboratory reagent water [CLRW], special reagent water [SRW] including molecular biology water, instrument feed water, and others) and does not use the term 'Type I'; the guideline and CAP text are not open and could not be read, so the > 10 MΩ·cm specification itself is unverified (one laboratory used it as its acceptance limit). Resistivity is an indicator of ionic contamination only: Liang 2024 documented a contaminant (suspected glycerol) after RO membrane replacement biasing triglyceride QC by +536%/+371% while resistivity stayed > 10 MΩ·cm. The reviewer's 95–99% RO removal differs from the 90–99% given for one system by Penna 2002.

evidence.citation: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute. GP40: Preparations and Testing of Reagent Water in the Medical Laboratory. 5th ed. 2024 (product page, read via a page-fetch tool)
Liang S, et al. Biochem Med (Zagreb). 2024;34(1):010705
Öztürk MA, et al. Sensors (Basel). 2025;25(4):1186
Penna VT, et al. BMC Public Health. 2002;2:13

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-reagent-water-ph-normality teaches the CLSI GP40 (2024) water-type names, presents > 10 MΩ·cm as one laboratory's acceptance limit, teaches 90–99% RO removal for one system, and stresses that resistivity reflects ions and misses organics and bacteria; lesson flags f-type-i-terminology and f-ro-removal.

flags.issue: The reviewer states [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 1 × 10⁻⁷ M and Kw = 10⁻¹⁴ for pure water without a temperature. These values hold at 25 °C (standard state); the pH of water is strongly temperature-dependent, and neutral water at 37 °C has pH 6.80.

evidence.citation: Steinegger A, et al. Chem Rev. 2020;120(22):12357-12489
Perlt E, et al. Sci Rep. 2017;7(1):10244

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-reagent-water-ph-normality teaches Kw = 10⁻¹⁴ and neutral pH 7 as 25 °C values and neutral pH 6.80 at 37 °C; lesson flag f-kw-temperature.

flags.issue: The reviewer states 2 M H₂SO₄ = 4 N without qualification. Normality depends on the reaction (n = H⁺ an acid actually donates or a base accepts), so 4 N holds only when both protons react. NIST SP 811 states that normality (N) and molarity (M) are obsolete and recommends amount-of-substance concentration in mol/L; Harvey notes normality is no longer in common use.

evidence.citation: Harvey D. Analytical Chemistry 2.1. Chemistry LibreTexts; Sections 2.2 and 16.1 (read via a page-fetch tool)
Thompson A, Taylor BN. Guide for the Use of the International System of Units (SI). NIST Special Publication 811. 2008 ed.; Sec. 8.6.5 (read via a page-fetch tool)

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-reagent-water-ph-normality teaches N = n × M with n = reacting protons, 2 M H₂SO₄ = 4 N only when both protons react, and that normality is obsolete; lesson flag f-normality-reaction.

flags.issue: Hit 12 (and Exam Trap 1) say lupus anticoagulant is 'mostly non-SLE' / 'mostly seen outside SLE'. The open sources read say only that LA was named after SLE and is also present in non-SLE disorders; none gave the proportion of LA-positive patients without SLE, so the 'mostly' claim is unverified.

evidence.citation: Vandevelde A, Devreese KMJ. J Clin Med. 2022;11(8):2164
Marco-Rico A. J Clin Med. 2025;14(8):2791

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-la-paradox-normal-screen-bleeding teaches that LA is named after SLE but not limited to it, and keeps 'mostly non-SLE' as a pending claim.

flags.issue: Trap 1 (and Hit 12) present LA-hypoprothrombinemia syndrome as a childhood bleeding syndrome that responds to corticosteroids. A case report with literature review states there are no treatment guidelines (corticosteroids remain the standard; 60% of 77 reviewed patients received them), drug- and infection-associated cases can resolve spontaneously, LAHPS is usually associated with autoimmune disease such as SLE, and thrombosis followed the initial bleeding presentation in 13% in another review.

evidence.citation: Omer MH, et al. Am J Case Rep. 2022;23:e938051
Sakamoto A, et al. Thromb J. 2021;19(1):19

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-la-paradox-normal-screen-bleeding teaches corticosteroids as the usual (not guideline-based) treatment, possible spontaneous resolution in infection-linked cases, and later thrombosis risk.

flags.issue: Hit 16 equates bleeding with normal platelets/PT/APTT/vWF with a vascular wall disorder. A state-of-the-art review lists vessel and connective-tissue mimics (scurvy, Ehlers-Danlos, vasculitis such as Henoch-Schönlein purpura, hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia) but also rare hyperfibrinolytic and natural-anticoagulant disorders missed by routine global tests, and reports that about 50-70% of patients with mild-to-moderate bleeding disorders remain a bleeding disorder of unknown cause after exclusion of VWD, factor deficiencies and platelet function defects.

evidence.citation: Mehic D, Pabinger I, Gebhart J. Res Pract Thromb Haemost. 2023;7(8):102242

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-la-paradox-normal-screen-bleeding teaches vessel-wall disorders and (rare) hyperfibrinolysis as two places to look, and that many normal-screen bleeders stay unexplained.

flags.issue: Hit 17 diagnoses hyperfibrinolysis from a short euglobulin lysis time. In a cohort study only five patients had a short baseline ECLT, whereas 37 were diagnosed through an increased ECLT ratio before and after venous compression; the ECLT is not available as a commercial test and fibrinolytic assays are not standardized. PAI-1 deficiency needs specific assays on morning samples, and PAI-1 antigen measurement is essential because current activity assays cannot reliably identify low values.

evidence.citation: Valke LLFG, et al. Res Pract Thromb Haemost. 2022;6(2):e12681
Haisma B, et al. Res Pract Thromb Haemost. 2026;10(6):106928

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-la-paradox-normal-screen-bleeding teaches specialised lysis testing (ECLT ratio, PAI-1 antigen and activity, alpha2-antiplasmin) and does not teach the 2-5 h ELT range.

flags.issue: Hit 11 defines myeloma as CRAB plus clonal marrow plasma cells. Since the 2014 IMWG revision, three biomarkers are also myeloma-defining events without CRAB: clonal marrow plasma cells of 60% or more, an involved:uninvolved serum free light chain ratio of 100 or more (involved FLC at least 100 mg/L), and more than one focal lesion of 5 mm or more on MRI. Myeloma also requires 10% or more clonal marrow plasma cells or a biopsy-proven plasmacytoma.

evidence.citation: Rajkumar SV. Am J Hematol. 2024;99(9):1802-1824 (read via a page-fetch tool)
Lakshman A, et al. Blood Cancer J. 2018;8(6):59

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-myeloma-wm-hodgkin-markers teaches CRAB cut-offs and the three biomarker events (exam trap "No CRAB = not myeloma").

flags.issue: Hit 11 (and the Number Vault) give smoldering myeloma progression as 10%/year for the first 5 years, then 3%, then 1%. This matches the smoldering section of Rajkumar 2024, whose introduction instead gives 1.5%/year after year 10, but the figure is not fixed. In a cohort meeting the 2014 IMWG criteria, progression was 18% in year 1, ~10%/year for the next 3 years and ~4%/year to 10 years, and it ranged from 5%/year (low risk) to 24%/year in the first 2 years (high risk: two or more of plasma cells >20%, M-protein >2 g/dL, FLC ratio >20).

evidence.citation: Rajkumar SV. Am J Hematol. 2024;99(9):1802-1824 (read via a page-fetch tool)
Lakshman A, et al. Blood Cancer J. 2018;8(6):59

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-myeloma-wm-hodgkin-markers teaches ~10%/year for 5 years then slower, the 2014-criteria cohort figures and the 20/2/20 risk factors.

flags.issue: Hit 13 pairs Waldenström macroglobulinemia with MYD88 L265P as if diagnostic. MYD88 L265P is detected in about 90-95% of WM by allele-specific PCR, but it is also present in about 50-90% of IgM MGUS, MYD88 mutations occur in ABC-type DLBCL, and lack of the mutation does not rule out lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma. WM is defined by an IgM M-protein of any size plus marrow lymphoplasmacytic infiltration.

evidence.citation: Bibas M, et al. Mediterr J Hematol Infect Dis. 2024;16(1):e2024061

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-myeloma-wm-hodgkin-markers teaches MYD88 L265P as supportive, not exclusive, and contrasts WM with IgM myeloma.

flags.issue: Hit 12 gives Reed-Sternberg cells as CD15+ without qualification and calls nodular sclerosis the young-women-with-mediastinal-mass subtype. HRS cells are universally CD30+ but only variably CD15+ (89% of cases by flow cytometry), lack CD45 and have reduced or absent CD20. Nodular sclerosis is described as mainly affecting adolescents with frequent mediastinal mass (70-80% of classic HL in Western countries); no female predominance was found in the sources read, so that part needs a primary source.

evidence.citation: Satou A, et al. Cancers (Basel). 2022;14(11):2647
Gajzer DC, et al. Cancers (Basel). 2025;17(5):814

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-myeloma-wm-hodgkin-markers teaches CD30+ (universal), CD15+ (most), CD45-; the sex predominance is a pending claim and is not taught.

flags.issue: Hit 3 (and the Number Vault) treats B12 deficiency as usually <100 ng/L and borderline as 100-200 ng/L. Nagao 2017 says deficiency is very likely below 200 pg/mL (= ng/L) and reserves metabolite testing for the 200-300 pg/mL zone; Wolffenbuttel 2019 uses 140-300 pmol/L as borderline; WHO adult cutoffs are <148 pmol/L deficient and 148-221 pmol/L low (Hannibal 2016). Serum B12 can also read normal or falsely high in pernicious anemia (Nagao 2017).

evidence.citation: Nagao T, Hirokawa M. J Gen Fam Med. 2017;18(5):200-204
Wolffenbuttel BHR, et al. Mayo Clin Proc Innov Qual Outcomes. 2019;3(2):200-214
Hannibal L, et al. Front Mol Biosci. 2016;3:27

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-macrocytic-b12-folate-hydroxyurea teaches <200 pg/mL very likely deficient, 200-300 pg/mL borderline (confirm with MMA), >300 unlikely, plus the WHO pmol/L cutoffs.

flags.issue: Hit 16 states hydroxyurea causes nonmegaloblastic macrocytosis with no hypersegmented neutrophils. Hydroxyurea inhibits ribonucleotide reductase and impairs DNA synthesis (Green 2014), and Nagao 2017 states macro-ovalocytes, anisocytosis and hypersegmented neutrophils may also be seen in drug-induced disorders of DNA synthesis; no source read states hydroxyurea macrocytosis lacks hypersegmented neutrophils. The discriminator is normal B12/folate plus the drug history, not the smear.

evidence.citation: Nagao T, Hirokawa M. J Gen Fam Med. 2017;18(5):200-204
Green NS, Barral S. Pediatr Res. 2014;75(1-2):196-204

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-macrocytic-b12-folate-hydroxyurea teaches hydroxyurea as a ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor that raises the MCV, and that smear features can overlap with megaloblastic anemia; the 'no hypersegmented neutrophils' claim is pending.

flags.issue: Hit 16 advises reviewing medications and TSH before chasing B12. Nagao 2017 begins the macrocytosis workup with serum B12, folate and the smear, and considers hypothyroidism (with alcohol, liver disease and MDS) once vitamin deficiency is excluded and reticulocytes are not raised. A medication history is appropriate, but B12 should not be deferred.

evidence.citation: Nagao T, Hirokawa M. J Gen Fam Med. 2017;18(5):200-204

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-macrocytic-b12-folate-hydroxyurea teaches measuring B12 and folate alongside the drug history; the TSH-first ordering is pending and not taught.

flags.issue: Hit 1 states normal marrow can raise red cell production 6-8x normal under extreme stimulation, without stating the iron condition. Hillman and Henderson 1969 (abstract; the article body on PMC is page images only) report an increase of as little as twice to as much as eight times normal depending on the iron pool: only two to three times normal with iron from normal reticuloendothelial stores or oral iron, and four to eight times only with iron from non-viable red cells, haemolysis or iron dextran infusion. The Number Vault note (full output needs parenteral iron) is consistent, but the hit omits it.

evidence.citation: Hillman RS, Henderson PA. Control of marrow production by the level of iron supply. J Clin Invest. 1969;48(3):454-460
Saito H. Metabolism of iron stores. Nagoya J Med Sci. 2014;76(3-4):235-254

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-marrow-reserve-23dpg-neocytolysis teaches the 2-3x vs 4-8x iron dependence; the Hct 0.35/0.25 doubling/tripling claim stays pending.

flags.issue: Hit 11 (and the Memory Hook 'Astronauts lose their neocytes', which says postflight) places neocytolysis in postflight astronauts. Risso 2014 places it in astronauts during the first days of spaceflight, when plasma volume falls about 20%, haematocrit rises, EPO declines and red cell mass falls 10-15%, and attributes the post-landing fall in haematocrit ('space anaemia') to the normal redistribution and re-expansion of blood fluid after return to normogravity.

evidence.citation: Risso A, Ciana A, Achilli C, Antonutto G, Minetti G. Neocytolysis: none, one or many? A reappraisal and future perspectives. Front Physiol. 2014;5:54
Mairbaurl H. Neocytolysis: How to Get Rid of the Extra Erythrocytes Formed by Stress Erythropoiesis Upon Descent From High Altitude. Front Physiol. 2018;9:345

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-marrow-reserve-23dpg-neocytolysis teaches neocytolysis early in flight and post-landing plasma re-expansion.

flags.issue: Hit 11 presents neocytolysis after EPO withdrawal as established. Risso 2014 calls it 'the hypothesis formulated to explain experimental evidence'; Mairbaurl 2018 states the mechanisms are unclear and might include withdrawal of EPO and impaired defence against reactive oxygen species (the EPO link resting on three subjects given EPO on descent), and that indications for neocytolysis after return from high altitude are weak.

evidence.citation: Mairbaurl H. Neocytolysis: How to Get Rid of the Extra Erythrocytes Formed by Stress Erythropoiesis Upon Descent From High Altitude. Front Physiol. 2018;9:345
Risso A, Ciana A, Achilli C, Antonutto G, Minetti G. Neocytolysis: none, one or many? A reappraisal and future perspectives. Front Physiol. 2014;5:54

flags.appAction: Lesson heme-marrow-reserve-23dpg-neocytolysis teaches neocytolysis as a proposed process with an unclear mechanism.

flags.issue: Hit 13 says sterile pyuria with haematuria in acidic urine should make you think of renal tuberculosis. Open sources list many other causes of sterile pyuria (recently treated UTI, Chlamydia, prostatitis, stones, neoplasms, catheters, drugs and drug-induced interstitial nephritis, pregnancy). They advise considering renal tuberculosis when sterile pyuria is chronic, especially with residence in an endemic region, immunosuppression or unintentional weight loss, and testing at least three consecutive early-morning urines by AFB culture (Kapoor 2008 prefers five). Acidic urine as a tuberculosis clue was not found in any source read.

evidence.citation: Glen P, et al. Br J Gen Pract. 2016;66(644):e225-e227
Mantica G, et al. Antibiotics (Basel). 2021;10(11):1399
Kapoor R, et al. Indian J Urol. 2008;24(3):401-405

flags.appAction: Lesson cm-urine-sterile-pyuria-dark-urine-galactosuria teaches the sterile pyuria differential and the early-morning AFB culture plan; the acidic-urine clue is left as a pending claim and not taught.

flags.issue: Hit 15 presents a positive reducing-sugar test with a negative glucose-oxidase result in a neonate as the galactosaemia clue, with no caveats. Reviews say the urine reducing-substance screen is neither sensitive nor specific: fructosuria, lactosuria (from intestinal lactase deficiency), and conditions that impair galactose clearance such as severe liver disease or antibiotic treatment give false positives, and intravenous feeding gives false negatives. The international guideline confirms classical galactosaemia by red-cell GALT activity and/or GALT gene analysis, and says to start a galactose-restricted diet immediately when it is suspected, without waiting for confirmation.

evidence.citation: Coelho AI, et al. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2017;40(3):325-342
Welling L, et al. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2017;40(2):171-176
Badiu Tișa I, et al. Nutrients. 2022;15(1):10

flags.appAction: Lesson cm-urine-sterile-pyuria-dark-urine-galactosuria teaches copper reduction vs glucose oxidase, the limits of the screen, GALT confirmation and an immediate diet change.

flags.issue: Hit 8 (and Trap 5) names the bicarbonate assay enzyme PEPCK (phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase). The enzymatic total CO2 assay described in an open evaluation uses phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase (PEPC) with Mg2+, which joins HCO3- and phosphoenolpyruvate to give oxaloacetate, followed by malate dehydrogenase; one evaluated kit reads an NADH analogue at 405 nm.

evidence.citation: Wei S, Fang Z, Shi M, et al. PLoS One. 2025;20(10):e0334228

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-coupled-nadh-alt-ast-bicarbonate teaches PEPC (carboxylase) and notes the reviewer's PEPCK wording.

flags.issue: Hit 8 and Trap 5 present LDH-related false elevation as a general property of the enzymatic bicarbonate assay. Saleem 2013 found it with specific recalled Olympus AU2700 reagent lots (>10% positive bias when LD >845 U/L; a later lot was unaffected) and concluded that very high LD may interfere with some enzymatic HCO3- assays. 2025 laboratory notices describe manufacturer-reported interference (one notice: a recall of certain Beckman Coulter bicarbonate reagent lots, up to 30% higher when LDH >600 U/L; another: 15-30% or greater positive bias in some patients with LDH >2,000 U/L). The effect is reagent- and lot-specific; one notice states blood gas analysis is not subject to it.

evidence.citation: Saleem M, Dimeski G, Bourne L, Coates P. Ann Clin Biochem. 2013;50(Pt 4):365-367 (abstract only)
Northwestern Medicine Laboratories. System Laboratory Update: LDH-Based Interference of Metabolic Panel Bicarbonate. 2025 (read via a page-fetch tool)
MUHC OPTILAB-CUSM. Memorandum: Bicarbonate - Assay Method Interference from LDH levels as of 600 U/L. 2025 (read via a page-fetch tool)

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-coupled-nadh-alt-ast-bicarbonate teaches LDH interference as reagent/lot-specific and confirms acid-base status by blood gas.

flags.issue: Hit 7 and Trap 6 say ALT and AST assays need pyridoxal phosphate and that B6 deficiency can blunt them, without noting that reagents are sold with and without P5P supplementation. The risk of missed elevations in vitamin B6 deficiency applies to non-supplemented reagents; in a 2023 CAP proficiency-testing survey only 38% (1651 of 4304) of responding laboratories reported using P5P-supplemented ALT and/or AST reagents.

evidence.citation: Chambliss AB, Souers RJ, Genzen JR, Manthei DM. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2025;149(5):400-404 (abstract only)

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-coupled-nadh-alt-ast-bicarbonate teaches that B6-related under-reading applies to reagents without added P5P.

flags.issue: Hit 13 states that in metabolic alkalosis PaCO2 rarely exceeds 60 mmHg. Open reviews give a different, source-dependent figure: Tinawi 2021 says PaCO2 is 'rarely over 55 mmHg', while Sood 2010 says compensatory PaCO2 'may rise higher than 55 mmHg'. The safer rule is to compare the measured PaCO2 with the expected value (0.7 x HCO3- + 21 +/- 2 per Sood 2010, or 40 + 0.6 x (HCO3- - 24) per Tinawi 2021); a higher PaCO2 indicates a coexisting respiratory acidosis.

evidence.citation: Tinawi M. Cureus. 2021;13(1):e12841
Sood P, et al. Indian J Crit Care Med. 2010;14(2):57-64

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-acid-base-hh-log-compensation-bohr does not teach the 60 mmHg figure; it teaches comparison with the expected-PaCO2 formula (worked case: HCO3- 40, PaCO2 58, above expected about 49-50) and cites Tinawi's 'rarely over 55 mmHg' as one review's figure.

flags.issue: Hit 13 says respiratory alkalosis has the most effective compensation of the four disorders without saying this applies to the chronic phase. Sood 2010 states that the maximum compensatory response is usually associated with only a 50-75% return of pH to normal and that in CHRONIC respiratory alkalosis the pH may completely return to normal in some cases; the acute renal response is small (HCO3- about -2 mEq/L per 10 mmHg fall in PaCO2 acutely vs -5 chronically, per Sood 2010 and Habib 2025).

evidence.citation: Sood P, et al. Indian J Crit Care Med. 2010;14(2):57-64
Habib T, et al. S Afr Fam Pract (2004). 2025;67(1):e1-e7

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-acid-base-hh-log-compensation-bohr teaches that only chronic respiratory alkalosis is described as able to normalise pH (in some cases) and gives the acute and chronic HCO3- responses.

flags.issue: Hit 8 says "Don't deliver <39 weeks without confirming [lung maturity] unless dates are certain" (and Exam Trap 5 frames FLM testing as the tool for the 32–39-week window), implying a mature FLM result justifies earlier delivery. Vanderhoeven 2014 found composite neonatal morbidity of 32.4% in neonates delivered before 39 weeks after a mature FLM result; after adjustment the composite outcome did not differ by FLM status (only RDS remained more frequent with immature/transitional results). Peppiatt 2024 reports FLM testing has declined as ACOG and NICHD set stricter indications for late-preterm and early-term birth, and that surfactant does not indicate maturity of other organ systems. The current ACOG committee opinion itself was not read.

evidence.citation: Vanderhoeven JP, et al. J Perinatol. 2014;34(4):322-325
Peppiatt I, et al. Acad Pathol. 2024;11(2):100115

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-fetal-lung-ffn-mca-doppler teaches that gestational age outweighs a mature L/S result and that a mature test before 39 weeks does not guarantee a well neonate; the reviewer's 39-week confirmation rule is not taught.

flags.issue: Hit 11 says MCA PSV >1.5 MoM "detects all fetal anemia (12% false-positive)". In Mari 2000 (summarised by Brennand 2009) MCA PSV had 100% sensitivity for moderate or severe anaemia with a 12% false-positive rate and did not predict mild anaemia; the DIAMOND study reported 88% sensitivity for severe anaemia; false positives increase after previous intrauterine transfusions (Brennand 2009), and after 36 weeks MCA PSV is more often falsely positive or negative (Pasman 2015).

evidence.citation: Brennand J. Australas J Ultrasound Med. 2009;12(3):35-38
Pasman SA, et al. Facts Views Vis Obgyn. 2015;7(2):129-136

flags.appAction: Lesson chem-fetal-lung-ffn-mca-doppler teaches >1.5 MoM as the threshold for moderate or severe anaemia (mild not predicted) leading to fetal blood sampling, with more false results after 36 weeks and after transfusion.

flags.issue: Hit 5 says the provider bears the risk of overruns under capitation, and Exam Trap 3 and the 5-Second Recall say the provider bears ALL the risk. Open payment-method reviews describe capitation as a transfer of risk to providers, but the Cochrane review says prospective fixed rates shift SOME financial risk from purchaser to provider, the Lancet Commission reports that most surveyed capitation systems adjust payments for health needs, and blended models pay selected services fee-for-service outside the capitation (carve-outs for high-priority services or those at risk of under-provision). The specific advice to carve out expensive esoteric molecular/genetic tests was not found in the sources read.

evidence.citation: Hanson K, et al. Lancet Glob Health. 2022;10(5):e715-e772
Yuan B, et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2017;3:CD011153
Obadha M, et al. Int J Health Plann Manage. 2019;34(1):e917-e933

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-capitation-leases-zero-based-budget teaches the risk shift to the provider without 'all', and carve-outs generically; the esoteric-test carve-out advice is listed as pending.

flags.issue: Hit 10 defines an operating lease by a 1-3 year term, maintenance included and no ownership, and a financial lease as noncancelable, maintenance-free, matching economic life and ending in ownership. Under ASC 842 (as summarized by an accounting firm; the Codification itself was not readable) a lease is a finance lease if ANY of five criteria is met: ownership transfer, a purchase option reasonably certain to be exercised, a term for the major part of remaining economic life, present value of payments substantially all of fair value, or a specialized asset with no alternative use; otherwise it is an operating lease. Ownership transfer and term relative to economic life are among the tests, but a term in years, maintenance and cancellability are not, and both kinds go on the lessee's balance sheet except certain leases of 12 months or less.

evidence.citation: BerryDunn. ASC 842 lease accounting standards: finance and operating leases. Updated June 2020
Mosca N, et al. Plast Reconstr Surg Glob Open. 2026;14(9):e8038

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-capitation-leases-zero-based-budget teaches the five ASC 842 criteria and the fair-market-value vs $1 buyout lease contrast; reviewer term/maintenance details are pending; US GAAP only.

flags.issue: Hit 11 contrasts zero-based budgeting with 'pro forma budgets built from baseline history' and says funding is justified anew each year. Walsh 2016 names the history-plus-adjustment method incremental budgeting, describes zero-based budgeting per budget cycle and notes cycles need not be annual; pro forma usually refers to forecasted financial statements (Mosca 2026). The terminology may mislead.

evidence.citation: Walsh K. Ann Med Health Sci Res. 2016;6(2):71-73
Mosca N, et al. Plast Reconstr Surg Glob Open. 2026;14(9):e8038

flags.appAction: Lesson ops-capitation-leases-zero-based-budget contrasts zero-based with incremental budgeting per budget cycle and does not use 'pro forma'.
